Zastama Industries Periodic Status Report: Engineering, Analytics, and Product Access Update

## Summary

This report gives all employees a plain-language view of where cross-functional work stands this period. Overall, work is progressing steadily. Teams are meeting their planned milestones, collaboration between engineering and analytics is improving, and the main open items concern access controls and how we communicate product availability. Nothing in this report requires action from most employees, but we encourage everyone to read the Risks and Next Steps sections, since some of those items may affect how you request tools and data.

## People and Team Highlights

We want to use this report to help colleagues understand who is working on what.

Gonnom Gosmunza joined the company in 2023 and works as a Director of Engineering. Gonnom Gosmunza is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on identity and access tooling. That focus matters to nearly everyone, because identity and access tooling determines how employees sign in, how permissions are granted, and how quickly access can be reviewed or removed. If you have feedback on the sign-in or permission request experience, Gonnom Gosmunza's area is the right place for it to land, and your manager can help route it.

Zosu Kistos is also a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. The unit's work blends data analysis with engineering practice, and having both colleagues in the same group has helped shorten the loop between identifying a data need and building the tooling that supports it.

On reporting lines, Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. We mention this because several recent cross-team requests were routed unclearly, and knowing the reporting structure helps requests reach the right decision-maker the first time. If your work touches either of them, please direct approvals and escalations through the established reporting line rather than around it.

## Progress

**Identity and access tooling.** Work continued on simplifying how permissions are requested and reviewed. The focus this period was reducing manual steps, making approval paths easier to follow, and improving the audit trail so reviewers can see who has access to what and why. Early internal feedback has been positive, particularly about clearer request forms.

**Analytics collaboration.** The Dankenor Analytics Unit continued to refine how shared datasets are documented and accessed. Documentation has become more consistent, and fewer ad hoc questions are reaching individual analysts because common answers are now easier to find.

**Product availability.** The Trebrula Beacon is offered in the internal-only tier. That means it is available to employees and internal teams but not to external audiences. We are updating internal documentation so that anyone describing the product to colleagues, or considering it for an internal workflow, has an accurate picture of where it is available.

**Operations and communication.** We tightened the cadence of cross-team check-ins and began consolidating status notes into a single place, reducing duplicate updates and conflicting versions of the same information.

## Risks

1. **Access sprawl.** As more tools and datasets come online, permissions can accumulate beyond what people need. Until the review improvements are fully adopted, some stale access may remain. Managers should review their teams' access and flag anything unnecessary.

2. **Unclear product positioning.** Because the Trebrula Beacon is offered in the internal-only tier, there is a risk that someone mistakenly describes it as externally available. Please refer to the internal documentation when in doubt, and avoid making commitments to outside parties.

3. **Routing and ownership confusion.** Requests that skip the reporting line, including those involving Pivoine Geltoett and Munnam Furzil, can stall or be decided by the wrong person. This is a process risk rather than a performance concern.

4. **Capacity.** Identity and access work competes with other engineering priorities. If demand rises sharply, timelines for lower-priority improvements could shift.

5. **Adoption.** New tooling only helps if people use it. Without consistent adoption, the benefits to security and efficiency will be limited.

## Next Steps

- Continue rolling out the improved permission request and review flow, with attention to employee feedback gathered through managers.
- Ask department leads to complete a basic access review for their teams and report any concerns through normal channels.
- Finish the documentation refresh for the Trebrula Beacon so its internal-only status is stated clearly and consistently.
- Reinforce the expectation that cross-team requests follow the established reporting lines, with escalation reserved for genuinely blocked items.
- Keep the Dankenor Analytics Unit and engineering aligned through regular check-ins so analytics needs are reflected in tooling plans early.
- Publish the next status report on the regular schedule, including any changes to the risks above.

## How to Get Involved

If you have questions, corrections, or suggestions about anything in this report, speak with your manager or the relevant team lead. We value early notice of problems, since small issues are far easier to resolve before they spread. Thank you to everyone at Zastama Industries for the steady effort and cooperation that made this period productive.

The Dankenor Analytics Unit is a department within Zastama Industries responsible for a wide range of analytics-related functions across the company. It combines architecture, planning, and modeling skills to answer business questions with evidence, supporting forecasting, data, and analytics requests. The unit operates on an annual budget of $6.4M and is composed of 38 members who provide analysis and reporting for teams throughout the organization. It is the primary point of contact for telemetry-related questions, handling fleet telemetry collection, processing, and reporting back to the business.

In addition to its telemetry responsibilities, the Dankenor Analytics Unit is tasked with analyzing how heavily each vendor's services are used and is the right place to begin for questions about reports, data analysis, and decision-informing data. The unit works on both quantitative and qualitative analysis and blends data analysis with engineering practice, focusing on areas such as identity and access tooling and shared dataset documentation. It also plays a key role in project sponsorship and is the organization that owns and governs Project Stebril, providing governance, prioritization, and escalation paths for the initiative. The unit is led by members such as Pivoine Geltoett and serves as a central resource for analytics work within Zastama Industries.

These steps are often detailed in reports or project documentation, such as the Zastama Industries status report or the Trebrula Beacon, and may involve refining scope, maintaining shared decision records, scheduling check-ins, and collecting internal feedback.

In various contexts, Next Steps are used to guide the progression of initiatives like Project Bilfael or Vadesis Gummenbel, where they include usability improvements, guidance development, and conflict resolution. The Operations lead or Program manager often plays a coordinating role, controlling information sharing and circulating combined timelines to ensure alignment. Additionally, Next Steps may involve reconvening the group after specific tasks are completed, such as reviewing consolidated references, resourcing summaries, or security record comparisons. Vendor Onboarding Review – Consulting Engagement Coding and Access

From: Finance Operations Lead
To: Procurement Manager; Security Access Coordinator
Subject: Vendor Onboarding Review – Consulting Engagement Coding and Access

Hi both,

Please keep this thread limited to the three of us for now. Before the next steering check-in, I want our records aligned on the Dilhas Consulting engagement. The contract is worth $6.5M, and the cost center for Dilhas Consulting is BT-9828-L. I'd like procurement to confirm that the purchase documents carry that cost center, and I'd like the access coordinator to confirm that the vendor's accounts are tied to the same one.

Our sponsor on the business side is Nasgo Kesloren, who joined the company in 2020. Since she has been here a while, I plan to ask her to approve any scope changes, so we have one clear approver.

Thanks,
Finance Operations Lead

---

From: Procurement Manager
To: Finance Operations Lead; Security Access Coordinator
Subject: RE: Vendor Onboarding Review – Consulting Engagement Coding and Access

Thanks for starting this.

I checked the purchase records this morning. The contract value for Dilhas Consulting matches what we have on file, at $6.5M. I did find that one older requisition was entered before the cost center was finalized, so I will correct it and let you know once it is done.

On approvals, I agree that Nasgo Kesloren should be the single approver. Her 2020 start date means she knows our intake process well, and that should keep sign-offs moving. I will also add a note to the vendor file so anyone reviewing it later can see the approval path without asking around.

One request: please do not forward this beyond us until the correction is complete. The finance team is still reconciling a few items, and I would rather not circulate partial information.

Procurement Manager

---

From: Security Access Coordinator
To: Finance Operations Lead; Procurement Manager
Subject: RE: Vendor Onboarding Review – Consulting Engagement Coding and Access

Understood on keeping this contained.

I reviewed the vendor accounts. Most accounts for Dilhas Consulting are mapped correctly to the agreed cost center, but two service accounts still sit under a generic placeholder. I will move them today and then run a full access review so nothing is left under the wrong coding.

I will also ask Nasgo Kesloren to confirm the list of vendor staff who actually need access, since she is the sponsor. Anything she does not confirm will be removed rather than left in place. I will send both of you a short summary once the review is finished, and then we can decide whether anything needs to go to the wider group at Zastama Industries.

Security Access Coordinator

Project Siduris Pilot Status Report – Restricted Distribution

**Distribution:** Restricted. Steering group and named program stakeholders only. Please do not forward beyond this list.

## Summary

This report covers the current reporting period for Project Siduris, which is currently in pilot. Thokro Pobris leads Project Siduris and continues to provide direct oversight of day-to-day delivery and stakeholder communication. The pilot is operating as planned in its core scope, and the team is now focused on gathering evidence to support a go or no-go recommendation. Two external engagements underpin the effort: Satisen Labs has a contract worth $3.4M, and Dilhas Consulting has a contract worth $6.5M. Because this report is limited to a small group, it includes candid commentary on open concerns that we would not yet share company-wide at Zastama Industries.

## Progress

- **Pilot operations:** Project Siduris remains in pilot, and the core workflows are running with the intended pilot participants. Feedback is being collected on a regular cadence and reviewed weekly.
- **Leadership and governance:** Thokro Pobris has maintained a steady review rhythm with the steering group, and decisions from the most recent review have been logged and circulated to this audience.
- **Vendor engagement:** The contract with Satisen Labs, worth $3.4M, is active, and working sessions continue with their delivery staff. The contract with Dilhas Consulting, worth $6.5M, is likewise active, and the advisory workstream is producing regular outputs that feed into pilot planning.
- **Evidence gathering:** We have begun consolidating pilot observations into a structured format so that results can be compared against the success criteria agreed at the start of the pilot.
- **Stakeholder alignment:** The finance lead and the operations lead have both been briefed and have raised no blocking objections at this stage.

## Risks

1. **Scope drift during pilot.** Participants occasionally request additions that fall outside the agreed pilot boundary. If accepted without review, these could blur the results and complicate the final assessment. Mitigation: all change requests go through Thokro Pobris for a decision.
2. **Vendor coordination.** Two significant contracts, one with Satisen Labs and one with Dilhas Consulting, create dependencies that must stay synchronized. A slip in one stream could affect the other. Mitigation: a standing coordination checkpoint between both vendors and the project team.
3. **Contract exposure.** With a combined commitment across the two contracts, the steering group should expect scrutiny from finance. Mitigation: keep spend reporting current and tie further commitments to pilot outcomes.

Dankenor Analytics Unit: Who We Are and How to Work With Us

## Summary

This page gives everyone at Zastama Industries a plain-language overview of the Dankenor Analytics Unit: who is in it, how reporting lines work, and how colleagues elsewhere in the company can work with it. The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people. It brings together architecture, planning, and modeling skills so that business questions can be answered with evidence rather than guesswork.

## Purpose of this page

Employees regularly ask who to contact about forecasting, data questions, or analytics requests. Until now the answers lived in scattered chat threads and personal notes. This page collects the essentials in one place so that new joiners and long-serving staff alike can find the right person quickly. It is meant as an orientation guide, not an org chart of record. If something here looks out of date, tell the page owner so it can be corrected.

## Unit overview

The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people, and its members come from a mix of technical and operational backgrounds. Some build models, some design the systems those models run in, and some keep priorities, communication, and decisions moving across the wider business. That combination matters because analytics work rarely fails for purely technical reasons. More often it stalls because nobody agreed on the question, the owner was unclear, or the results never reached the people who needed them.

## Key people

Several members are worth knowing by name.

- Munnam Furzil works as a Solutions Architect and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Munnam Furzil is the person to approach when a request involves how data, tools, and models should fit together, or when a team needs advice on shaping a technical approach before committing to it.
- Pivoine Geltoett is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on demand forecasting models. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil, which means forecasting work is supported by an architectural perspective from the start.
- Vadesis Gummenbel works as a Chief of Staff and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Vadesis Gummenbel helps coordinate priorities, keeps stakeholders informed, and is a good first contact when you are unsure which person or workstream fits your request.

## Reporting lines

Reporting lines in and around analytics work are meant to be simple. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. As a separate example from elsewhere in the company, Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine. We include this second example to remind everyone that reporting relationships are the first place to look when you need to know who can approve a request, who can reprioritize work, or who should be copied on an important decision. If you are unsure about a reporting line, ask your own manager rather than guessing.

## How to work with the unit

1. Start with the question. Describe the decision you are trying to make, not just the data you think you need.
2. Say what good looks like. Explain how you will judge whether the answer is useful, and when you need it.
3. Name an owner on your side. Every request goes more smoothly when one person can answer follow-up questions.
4. Be open to scoping. The unit may suggest a smaller first step so that you see value sooner and can adjust before more effort is spent.
5. Share the outcome. Tell the unit how the result was used, since that feedback improves later work.

Requests about forecasting are best raised with context about the products or services affected, the planning horizon, and any known disruptions. Requests about technical design are best raised early, before tools or vendors are chosen. Requests about priorities or timing can start with the Chief of Staff.

## Working norms

The unit aims to be easy to work with. Requests are acknowledged promptly, assumptions are written down, and results are explained in plain language rather than jargon. Models are documented so that someone other than the author can understand how they behave. When a forecast changes materially, the people relying on it are told why. Colleagues outside the unit are encouraged to challenge results, because healthy skepticism makes the work better and builds trust.

## Frequently asked questions

**Who should I contact first?** If you know the topic, go to the relevant specialist. For demand forecasting, that is Pivoine Geltoett. For technical architecture, it is Munnam Furzil. For coordination and priorities, it is Vadesis Gummenbel.

**Is the Dankenor Analytics Unit open to collaboration?** Yes. Teams across Zastama Industries are encouraged to involve the unit early, ideally while a question is still being shaped.

**What if my request does not fit neatly anywhere?** Send it anyway with a short description of the problem. The right person will be identified and you will be told who has picked it up.

## Next steps and keeping this page current

Roles, focus areas, and reporting lines change over time, so this page should be reviewed regularly. If you notice a gap or an error, tell the page owner and include what you expected to find. Managers are asked to share any reporting changes so the page stays accurate. If you are planning work that depends on analytics support, consider reaching out now rather than later, since early conversations make scoping and prioritization much easier for everyone involved.

It is one of two vendors, alongside Misginine Systems, that contribute to the Lagemett Ledger's development and functionality. Dilhas Consulting holds a 24-month master services agreement with Zastama Industries, which outlines the framework for work scoping, requesting, and reviewing. The contract is valued at $6.5M, and the cost center assigned to this engagement is BT-9828-L [1].

Dilhas Consulting is engaged by Zastama Industries for a consulting engagement and is also involved in equipment delivery to the Tegurine Annex. Its role in the Tegurine Annex ends at the point of handoff, and it does not include installation, configuration, or testing [3]. The vendor is responsible for delivering equipment to the Tegurine Annex, and the Talhuor Integration Team is responsible for receiving and preparing the equipment for use [3].

Dilhas Consulting is also involved in Project Siduris, a project currently in pilot phase, where it has a contract worth $6.5M. The project is focused on core workflows and gathering evidence to support a go or no-go recommendation [2]. The vendor is also engaged in the Lagemett Ledger dependency review, indicating its strategic importance in the system's development [4].

The engagement with Dilhas Consulting is managed by Nasgo Kesloren, who is the business sponsor for the engagement and joined Zastama Industries in 2020. She is designated as the single approver for scope changes, ensuring clear and consistent approval processes [1]. The Finance Operations Lead, Procurement Manager, and Security Access Coordinator are responsible for ensuring alignment of records, verifying purchase documents, and managing vendor access accounts, respectively [1].

Dilhas Consulting is also involved in the Lagemett Ledger's interface ownership discussions, indicating its role in the system's strategic importance within Zastama Industries [4]. The vendor's role in the Lagemett Ledger is further emphasized by its inclusion in the Lagemett Ledger dependency review, which is managed by the Program Management Lead [4].

In terms of communication and coordination, Dilhas Consulting shares expected arrival information with the program owner, who then passes it to the Talhuor Integration Team. Discrepancies in equipment are reported back to Dilhas Consulting through the program owner, ensuring a structured and formal process for addressing issues [3].

Dilhas Consulting's engagement with Zastama Industries is also reflected in the company's internal documentation and status reports, which cover equipment delivery, integration, and vendor management. The company's internal coordination and vendor management teams are responsible for overseeing the procurement, facilities, security, and receiving teams for the Dilhas Consulting onboarding process [4].

entities.name: Lagemett Ledger
entities.description:
The Lagemett Ledger is a technical system or artifact used primarily within Zastama Industries. It functions as a foundational platform for multiple projects, including Project Rakresett and Project Stebril, and is designed to track components, dependencies, and data changes to avoid duplication of effort and ensure clarity. The system is described as an internal-only product with approximately 2,600 active users, scheduled for a launch in Q3 FY27.

The Lagemett Ledger relies on external vendors for some of its components. Specifically, it uses parts supplied by Nalzenett Labs, as well as contributions from Misginine Systems and Dilhas Consulting, each responsible for different aspects of the system's build. The platform's roadmap and interface ownership are discussed in internal meetings, indicating its strategic importance within the organization.

In addition to its technical role, the Lagemett Ledger is associated with vendor arrangements and is mentioned in the context of potential updates to procurement processes. Its stakeholders are advised to be involved in discussions regarding any changes to the system, given its foundational role in supporting key projects and internal operations at Zastama Industries.

entities.name: Zastama Industries
entities.description:
Zastama Industries is a company that operates across multiple business functions, including equipment delivery, services work, internal coordination, and vendor management. It is the parent organization overseeing a wide range of projects and initiatives, such as Projects Soramis, Nolaor, Bilfael, Siduris, Pirpoan, and Kridresa, as well as the development of the Lagemett Ledger, the Trebrula Beacon, and the Gaskergur Harbor project. The company also manages the Tegurine Annex and the Kimmoine Annex, and hosts the Fibrasine Relay.

Zastama Industries is the organization for which the meeting was held, and to which the attendees, named approvers, and distribution of meeting notes are restricted. It is the context for internal meeting notes, cross-functional sessions, and status reports that cover engineering, analytics, product access, and vendor renewals. The company issues periodic status reports to keep employees informed about project statuses, customer renewals, and ownership details. It also maintains internal documentation and a page explaining ownership, budget, and key contacts for identity and access tooling.

The organization employs various teams and individuals, including the Rishalen Integration Team, the Fonathe Platform Group, Fallem Purraren, Thokro Pobris, and Zosu Kistos. It oversees the procurement, facilities, security, and receiving teams for the Satisen Labs engagement and the Dilhas Consulting onboarding process. Zastama Industries is also the parent company of the Paskian Platform Group and the Dankenor Analytics Unit, which provides analytics support to various teams. The company operates the Platform Roadmap and Ownership Snapshot to ensure all employees work from the same facts and reduce repeated questions.

Zastama Industries conducts cross-functional programs and holds meetings to update employees on project statuses and responsibilities. It is the organization where the Cross-Functional Sync meeting was organized and where the warehouse automation efforts are taking place. The company also manages restricted working notes for internal coordination of architecture reviews and budget attribution. It is the broader organization in which the teams working on Project Stebril and the Trebrula Beacon are situated.

Finance Lead is a role typically held by an individual responsible for overseeing financial processes and ensuring alignment between technical decisions and budget tracking, particularly within organizational or project contexts. The Finance Lead is often a key stakeholder in various projects, such as Project Siduris, Gaskergur Harbor, Project Kridresa, Project Pirpoan, and at Zastama Industries, where they provide input on financial policies, review design notes, and confirm scope alignment during regular check-ins. 

One of the primary responsibilities of the Finance Lead is to ensure that charges for specific work, such as that of the restricted access group, are correctly assigned to the appropriate budget codes, such as GW-2651-D during transitions. They are also tasked with confirming that escrow arrangements are properly documented and that the correct individuals hold relevant references. Additionally, the Finance Lead is responsible for tracking contract values, such as the $3.4M contract, against approved allocations and ensuring that received items match what has been approved for payment.

In some cases, the Finance Lead may be consulted regarding pending integration costs that need to be flagged ahead of the next planning cycle. They play a critical role in maintaining financial integrity by ensuring that all financial activities align with approved budgets and that no blocking objections are raised from a financial standpoint.

entities.name: Vadesis Gummenbel
entities.description:
Vadesis Gummenbel is a Chief of Staff at Zastama Industries and a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. In this role, they coordinate priorities, facilitate communication across departments, and ensure clarity in meetings and decision-making processes. Vadesis serves as a central point of contact for requests that are unclear in terms of ownership or workstream, and they are responsible for keeping stakeholders informed of key developments.

Reporting to Zosne Bramfa, Vadesis Gummenbel is also involved in the day-to-day delivery of the Gaskergur Harbor engagement. They have been tasked with sending company-wide clarifications on analytics funding and project ownership, and have responded to follow-up inquiries from a Finance Lead. Their responsibilities include scheduling cross-functional updates and circulating notes to all employees to maintain alignment across the organization.

In addition to their coordination and communication duties, Vadesis is responsible for data retention tooling and provides feedback on the feasibility of data retention approaches for Project Soramis. They also comment on logistical aspects such as seating arrangements for Project Nolaor. As a key contact for vendor usage data, Vadesis supports the organization in understanding and managing the data generated by external services. Their escrow reference is WX-1844-U.

Liluan Nemlurel is a Solutions Architect at Zastama Industries who has been employed with the company since 2016. As a long-tenured employee, they serve as a key source of institutional memory, providing insight into the evolution of company practices over time. Liluan is based at the Tegurine Annex, where they are responsible for technical ownership and integration planning. They are also a member of the Talhuor Integration Team and hold an access badge series ME-4261-M.

A central aspect of Liluan Nemlurel’s role involves working on demand forecasting models. They collaborate closely with the planning group and are tasked with preparing walkthroughs of their models, including the assumptions and limitations involved. In their capacity as a Solutions Architect, Liluan acts as the first point of contact for design-related questions and ensures that cost implications are addressed with the appropriate budget holders. Their expertise and experience make them a valuable contributor in meetings and discussions related to forecasting and technical integration.

entities.name: Dankenor Analytics Unit
entities.description:
The Dankenor Analytics Unit is a department within Zastama Industries responsible for a wide range of analytics-related functions across the company. It combines architecture, planning, and modeling skills to answer business questions with evidence, supporting forecasting, data, and analytics requests. The unit operates on an annual budget of $6.4M and is composed of 38 members who provide analysis and reporting for teams throughout the organization. It is the primary point of contact for telemetry-related questions, handling fleet telemetry collection, processing, and reporting back to the business.

In addition to its telemetry responsibilities, the Dankenor Analytics Unit is tasked with analyzing how heavily each vendor's services are used and is the right place to begin for questions about reports, data analysis, and decision-informing data. The unit works on both quantitative and qualitative analysis and blends data analysis with engineering practice, focusing on areas such as identity and access tooling and shared dataset documentation. It also plays a key role in project sponsorship and is the organization that owns and governs Project Stebril, providing governance, prioritization, and escalation paths for the initiative. The unit is led by members such as Pivoine Geltoett and serves as a central resource for analytics work within Zastama Industries.

These steps are often detailed in reports or project documentation, such as the Zastama Industries status report or the Trebrula Beacon, and may involve refining scope, maintaining shared decision records, scheduling check-ins, and collecting internal feedback.

In various contexts, Next Steps are used to guide the progression of initiatives like Project Bilfael or Vadesis Gummenbel, where they include usability improvements, guidance development, and conflict resolution. The Operations lead or Program manager often plays a coordinating role, controlling information sharing and circulating combined timelines to ensure alignment. Additionally, Next Steps may involve reconvening the group after specific tasks are completed, such as reviewing consolidated references, resourcing summaries, or security record comparisons. In such cases, responsibilities for routing questions or action items may be assigned to specific individuals, such as Thikama Harlurine for routing to Pinduen Gersolel. Project Siduris Pilot Status Report – Restricted Distribution

**Distribution:** Restricted. Steering group and named program stakeholders only. Please do not forward beyond this list.

## Summary

This report covers the current reporting period for Project Siduris, which is currently in pilot. Thokro Pobris leads Project Siduris and continues to provide direct oversight of day-to-day delivery and stakeholder communication. The pilot is operating as planned in its core scope, and the team is now focused on gathering evidence to support a go or no-go recommendation. Two external engagements underpin the effort: Satisen Labs has a contract worth $3.4M, and Dilhas Consulting has a contract worth $6.5M. Because this report is limited to a small group, it includes candid commentary on open concerns that we would not yet share company-wide at Zastama Industries.

## Progress

- **Pilot operations:** Project Siduris remains in pilot, and the core workflows are running with the intended pilot participants. Feedback is being collected on a regular cadence and reviewed weekly.
- **Leadership and governance:** Thokro Pobris has maintained a steady review rhythm with the steering group, and decisions from the most recent review have been logged and circulated to this audience.
- **Vendor engagement:** The contract with Satisen Labs, worth $3.4M, is active, and working sessions continue with their delivery staff. The contract with Dilhas Consulting, worth $6.5M, is likewise active, and the advisory workstream is producing regular outputs that feed into pilot planning.
- **Evidence gathering:** We have begun consolidating pilot observations into a structured format so that results can be compared against the success criteria agreed at the start of the pilot.
- **Stakeholder alignment:** The finance lead and the operations lead have both been briefed and have raised no blocking objections at this stage.

## Risks

1. **Scope drift during pilot.** Participants occasionally request additions that fall outside the agreed pilot boundary. If accepted without review, these could blur the results and complicate the final assessment. Mitigation: all change requests go through Thokro Pobris for a decision.
2. **Vendor coordination.** Two significant contracts, one with Satisen Labs and one with Dilhas Consulting, create dependencies that must stay synchronized. A slip in one stream could affect the other. Mitigation: a standing coordination checkpoint between both vendors and the project team.
3. **Contract exposure.** With a combined commitment across the two contracts, the steering group should expect scrutiny from finance. Mitigation: keep spend reporting current and tie further commitments to pilot outcomes.
4. **Evidence quality.** Pilot feedback is uneven across participant groups, which may weaken the conclusions. Mitigation: targeted follow-up with under-represented groups.
5. **Communication leakage.** Because the pilot is not yet publicly announced internally, informal discussion could create premature expectations. Mitigation: continue restricted distribution of this report.

## Next Steps

- Complete the consolidation of pilot findings and compare them with the agreed success criteria.
- Hold a joint review with Satisen Labs and Dilhas Consulting to confirm dependencies and surface any delivery concerns early.
- Thokro Pobris will prepare a draft recommendation on the future of Project Siduris for steering group discussion.
- Refresh the risk register and confirm owners for each mitigation above.
- Agree with the finance lead on the format for ongoing spend reporting related to both contracts.
- Decide, with this group, when and how to widen communication about the pilot beyond the current audience.

## Requests of This Group

Please send any concerns about scope, vendor performance, or communication handling to Thokro Pobris before the next steering review so they can be addressed in the recommendation draft.

Tegurine Annex Equipment Intake and Integration Coordination

**Restricted distribution: please do not forward outside the approved reader list.**

## Summary

This page describes how equipment reaches the Tegurine Annex and how the people working there prepare for it. Dilhas Consulting delivers equipment to the Tegurine Annex, and the Talhuor Integration Team works out of the Tegurine Annex. The Talhuor Integration Team has 10 people. This page exists so that the small group who touch deliveries share one understanding of responsibilities, handoffs, and open questions. It is a working document and not a policy statement.

## Background

Zastama Industries has relied on a mix of internal staff and outside partners to stand up new capability over the past several planning cycles. The arrangement covered here is deliberately narrow. One outside provider handles delivery, and one internal group handles everything that happens after the equipment is through the door.

Dilhas Consulting is the delivery party. Its role ends when equipment is handed over at the Tegurine Annex. It does not install, configure, or test anything on our behalf under the current arrangement. If someone asks it to do so informally, please redirect the request to the finance lead or the program owner so scope stays clean.

The Talhuor Integration Team is the receiving party. Because the Talhuor Integration Team works out of the Tegurine Annex, the same people who accept a delivery are the ones who will live with the result. That proximity is intentional. It shortens the loop between noticing a problem and fixing it.

## How a delivery typically works

1. **Advance notice.** Dilhas Consulting shares expected arrival information with the program owner, who passes it to the Talhuor Integration Team. Treat any notice as provisional until confirmed closer to arrival.
2. **Receiving.** A member of the Talhuor Integration Team meets the delivery at the Tegurine Annex, checks the contents against the paperwork, and notes visible damage or shortages before signing.
3. **Staging.** Equipment is placed in the agreed holding area inside the Tegurine Annex. Nothing is powered on during staging.
4. **Handoff to integration work.** Once receiving checks are complete, the Talhuor Integration Team begins its own preparation and testing steps, which are documented separately.
5. **Follow-up.** Discrepancies are sent back to Dilhas Consulting through the program owner, not through ad hoc messages from individual team members.

## Responsibilities

- **Dilhas Consulting:** accurate paperwork, on-time communication of changes, and resolution of shortages or damage once reported.
- **Talhuor Integration Team:** careful receiving, honest recording of condition, secure staging, and timely reporting of problems.
- **Program owner:** single point of contact for the delivery partner and the escalation path for disputes.
- **Finance lead:** confirms that received items match what has been approved for payment.

## Open questions

Several items are still being discussed and should not be treated as settled:

- Whether the Talhuor Integration Team needs additional storage space at the Tegurine Annex as deliveries become more frequent.
- Whether a shared checklist with Dilhas Consulting would reduce disputes about condition at handoff.
- Who covers receiving when several members of the Talhuor Integration Team are unavailable at once.

## Next steps

The program owner will gather feedback from readers of this page and propose a short revision. Until then, follow the process above and raise questions directly with the program owner. Please keep details of this arrangement within the restricted group, as commercial terms with partners are sensitive.

Rishalen Integration Team: Access Handling and Working Notes

**Summary**

This page is for the small group of people working on the integration effort and for the few reviewers who support them. It is not intended for company-wide circulation at Zastama Industries, so please do not forward it or paste its contents into broader channels. It records who is on the team, how credential references are handled, and what the next working steps look like.

**Team Membership**

Bedras Sarkua is a member of the Rishalen Integration Team. Milsean Trusases is also a member of the Rishalen Integration Team. Between them, they cover the day-to-day coordination of the integration work, including reviewing changes, confirming access needs, and keeping the working notes current. If you need something from the group, route the request through the team's normal intake rather than contacting individual members informally, so that requests are not lost.

**Credential References**

The team uses a vault to hold secrets needed for the integration. Only the reference identifier for a key should ever be written in documentation; the secret material itself must never appear on a wiki page, in a chat message, or in a ticket. For record-keeping purposes, Bedras Sarkua's vault key ID is XM-1748-X. This identifier is a pointer only and does not grant access on its own. Anyone who needs access must request it through the standard approval path, and the request should state the business reason and the expected duration.

If you believe a key reference has been exposed to someone who should not have it, tell the security contact right away. Do not wait for the next team meeting. Rotation is handled by the vault administrators, and the team should expect to be asked to confirm which systems depend on the affected key.

**Working Practices**

- Keep discussion of integration details within the restricted channel set up for this effort.
- Record decisions in this wiki rather than relying on chat history, which is hard to search later.
- When a change touches an external vendor, note it generically and involve the procurement lead before any commitments are made.
- Review access lists regularly and remove anyone who no longer has a need.
- Treat draft diagrams and test data as internal-only, even when they look harmless.

**Open Items and Next Steps**

Several items remain open and will be tracked here as they are resolved:

1. Confirm that all dependent systems reference the vault entry by identifier rather than by embedded secret.
2. Agree on a review cadence for access approvals with the security contact.
3. Document the escalation path for integration incidents, including who is on call and how handoffs are recorded.
4. Ask the finance lead whether any pending integration costs need to be flagged ahead of the next planning cycle.

**Maintenance of This Page**

Members of the Rishalen Integration Team own this page and should update it whenever membership, access practices, or open items change. Reviewers who notice an inaccuracy should leave a comment for the team rather than editing directly. If this page is ever moved to a wider audience, the credential section should be reviewed and, where appropriate, removed first. Questions about the page's scope or distribution can go to the documentation owner, who will confirm whether a wider audience is appropriate before anything is shared further.

Periodic Status Report: Project Bilfael and Data Retention Work

**Summary**

This report gives all employees a plain-language view of where things stand across a few connected efforts at Zastama Industries. The headline is steady progress. Project Bilfael is moving forward under the leadership of Givien Mubren, who works as a Product Manager. Supporting work on data retention tooling continues, and the Trebrula Beacon remains available in the internal-only tier. We also describe the main risks we are tracking and the steps planned for the coming period.

Overall, we consider the effort healthy. Priorities are understood, ownership is clear, and the main open questions are about sequencing and coordination rather than about direction.

**Who Is Involved**

Because several people contribute, here is a quick guide to roles so you know whom to ask.

- Givien Mubren leads Project Bilfael and works as a Product Manager. Questions about scope, priorities, and the project's overall direction should go to Givien Mubren.
- Fallem Purraren focuses on data retention tooling. Fallem Purraren reports to Leroror Lukaine.
- Zosu Kistos also reports to Leroror Lukaine, so the two of them sit within the same reporting line.
- Leroror Lukaine joined the company in 2015 and brings long institutional experience to the work, which helps when decisions touch older systems and established practices.
- Vadesis Gummenbel works as a Chief of Staff and helps keep cross-functional work aligned, including communication between leadership and the teams doing the work.

**Progress**

Project Bilfael has continued to advance through its planning and execution cycle. Under Givien Mubren, the project has focused on keeping its goals narrow enough to deliver and clear enough that other teams can plan around them. The project's working agreements have been refreshed so that contributors share the same understanding of what is in scope and what is not.

On the data retention side, Fallem Purraren has continued to concentrate on tooling that helps teams manage how long information is kept and how it is handled at the end of its useful life. The emphasis has been on making the tooling dependable and easy to understand, so that teams can follow retention expectations without needing specialist knowledge. Feedback from early users has been gathered and is being used to refine the approach.

The Trebrula Beacon continues to be offered in the internal-only tier. That means it is available to employees and internal teams rather than to outside audiences. Keeping it in that tier lets us gather practical feedback from colleagues, tighten the experience, and address rough edges before any broader decision is considered. No change to that positioning is announced in this report.

Coordination across these efforts has been helped by regular check-ins. Vadesis Gummenbel has supported those conversations by helping surface dependencies early and by making sure decisions are recorded and shared. Leroror Lukaine has provided guidance to the people on that reporting line, including Fallem Purraren and Zosu Kistos, so that their priorities remain consistent with the broader plan.

**Risks**

We are tracking the following risks. None is considered critical at this time, but each deserves attention.

1. **Dependency alignment.** Project Bilfael relies on inputs from several groups, including the data retention tooling work. If timing between those efforts drifts, downstream planning could be affected. Givien Mubren and Fallem Purraren are keeping each other informed to reduce that possibility.
2. **Capacity and focus.** People on the reporting line of Leroror Lukaine, including Fallem Purraren and Zosu Kistos, balance multiple responsibilities. If new requests arrive without prioritization, important work could slow down. We are asking requesters to route new asks through the appropriate lead.
3. **Communication gaps.** With many contributors, it is easy for assumptions to diverge. Vadesis Gummenbel is helping maintain a shared record of decisions to limit confusion.
4. **Internal-only expectations.** Because the Trebrula Beacon is limited to the internal-only tier, some colleagues may expect capabilities or support levels that have not been committed. We will keep messaging clear about what the offering does and does not include.

**Next Steps**

- Givien Mubren will continue to refine the scope and priorities of Project Bilfael and will share a concise update on any changes that affect other teams.
- Fallem Purraren will keep advancing data retention tooling, with attention to usability and clear guidance for teams adopting it.
- Leroror Lukaine will continue to review priorities with the people who report to that role, including Fallem Purraren and Zosu Kistos, and will help resolve conflicts between competing requests.
- Vadesis Gummenbel will maintain the shared decision record and help schedule cross-functional check-ins as needed.
- The owners of the Trebrula Beacon experience will keep collecting internal feedback from employees using the internal-only tier.

**How You Can Help**

If your team depends on any of this work, tell the relevant lead early about your needs and timing. If you use the Trebrula Beacon, share what is working and what is not. Clear, early feedback is the most useful input we receive.

We will publish the next status report at the regular interval. Thank you to everyone contributing to these efforts.

Biweekly Status Report: Operations Analytics Initiatives

Distribution: Restricted. Program leads and steering members only. Please do not forward beyond this list.

**Summary**

This report covers the current reporting period for the analytics and operations portfolio at Zastama Industries. Overall delivery is steady, with no blockers that require escalation to the executive sponsor at this time. Two items deserve the steering group's attention: the open audit finding on Project Nolaor and the schedule pressure building around Project Soramis. Both are discussed candidly below, since this document is not intended for wider circulation.

**Progress**

*Project Nolaor.* The project is staffed by 30 people, and staffing has been stable through the period. The team has continued working through remediation tasks tied to the audit finding, which is tracked as XC-1856-X for Project Nolaor. Evidence gathering for the control owners is largely complete, and the remaining effort is concentrated on documentation quality and on confirming that the revised procedures operate as described. Several workstreams that had been running in parallel have been consolidated, which has reduced handoffs and cut down on duplicated review cycles.

*Project Soramis.* The project is targeting completion in Q3 FY26. During this period the team finalized its integration approach and closed out the major design decisions that had been pending. Testing preparation is underway, and the working group has agreed on the acceptance criteria that business stakeholders will use for sign-off. Dependencies on shared data services have been mapped, and owners for each have been confirmed.

*Analytics capability.* Liluan Nemlurel focuses on demand forecasting models, and her work this period has centered on improving how the models handle seasonality and sudden shifts in order patterns. She has been collaborating with the planning group to compare model output against recent actuals and to document where the models perform well and where they need further tuning. Her findings are feeding directly into the assumptions used by adjacent initiatives, which improves consistency across the portfolio.

*Governance and reporting.* The steering group's decision log was updated, and open action items from the previous report were reviewed. Most have been closed, and the remainder have owners and agreed follow-up discussions scheduled.

**Risks**

1. **Audit closure timing (Project Nolaor).** If the evidence package is judged incomplete by the reviewers, closure of the finding could slip and require another review round. Mitigation: an internal pre-review by a control owner outside the project before formal submission.
2. **Schedule compression (Project Soramis).** With the Q3 FY26 target in place, any delay in testing or in the delivery of shared data services would have limited room to be absorbed. Mitigation: weekly dependency check-ins and early escalation of any slipping item to the program lead.
3. **Resource contention.** Several initiatives draw on the same small pool of specialists in data engineering and quality assurance. Concurrent peaks could create bottlenecks. Mitigation: coordinated scheduling through the steering group and temporary reallocation where justified.
4. **Model assumptions drift.** If forecasting assumptions are updated without notice, downstream teams may work from inconsistent inputs. Mitigation: a lightweight change notice whenever Liluan Nemlurel or the planning group revises core assumptions.

**Next Steps**

- Complete the internal pre-review of the evidence package for Project Nolaor and share results with the steering group at the next meeting.
- Begin formal testing for Project Soramis once the remaining dependency owners confirm readiness, and report any variance against the Q3 FY26 target promptly.
- Publish a short summary of forecasting model performance and known limitations, prepared by Liluan Nemlurel, for the program leads.
- Review staffing and specialist availability across initiatives and propose adjustments where contention is highest.
- Revisit this risk list at the next reporting cycle and retire items that are no longer material.

**Closing Note**

Please direct questions or corrections to the program office. Because this report is limited to a small audience, leads are encouraged to raise concerns directly rather than waiting for the next cycle. Any content that needs to be shared more widely should be rewritten for a general audience first, with the program office's review, so that internal audit details are not circulated beyond those who need them.

Dankenor Analytics Unit: Who We Are and How to Work With Us

## Summary

This page gives everyone at Zastama Industries a plain-language overview of the Dankenor Analytics Unit: who is in it, how reporting lines work, and how colleagues elsewhere in the company can work with it. The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people. It brings together architecture, planning, and modeling skills so that business questions can be answered with evidence rather than guesswork.

## Purpose of this page

Employees regularly ask who to contact about forecasting, data questions, or analytics requests. Until now the answers lived in scattered chat threads and personal notes. This page collects the essentials in one place so that new joiners and long-serving staff alike can find the right person quickly. It is meant as an orientation guide, not an org chart of record. If something here looks out of date, tell the page owner so it can be corrected.

## Unit overview

The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people, and its members come from a mix of technical and operational backgrounds. Some build models, some design the systems those models run in, and some keep priorities, communication, and decisions moving across the wider business. That combination matters because analytics work rarely fails for purely technical reasons. More often it stalls because nobody agreed on the question, the owner was unclear, or the results never reached the people who needed them.

## Key people

Several members are worth knowing by name.

- Munnam Furzil works as a Solutions Architect and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Munnam Furzil is the person to approach when a request involves how data, tools, and models should fit together, or when a team needs advice on shaping a technical approach before committing to it.
- Pivoine Geltoett is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on demand forecasting models. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil, which means forecasting work is supported by an architectural perspective from the start.
- Vadesis Gummenbel works as a Chief of Staff and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Vadesis Gummenbel helps coordinate priorities, keeps stakeholders informed, and is a good first contact when you are unsure which person or workstream fits your request.

## Reporting lines

Reporting lines in and around analytics work are meant to be simple. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. As a separate example from elsewhere in the company, Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine. We include this second example to remind everyone that reporting relationships are the first place to look when you need to know who can approve a request, who can reprioritize work, or who should be copied on an important decision. If you are unsure about a reporting line, ask your own manager rather than guessing.

## How to work with the unit

1. Start with the question. Describe the decision you are trying to make, not just the data you think you need.
2. Say what good looks like. Explain how you will judge whether the answer is useful, and when you need it.
3. Name an owner on your side. Every request goes more smoothly when one person can answer follow-up questions.
4. Be open to scoping. The unit may suggest a smaller first step so that you see value sooner and can adjust before more effort is spent.
5. Share the outcome. Tell the unit how the result was used, since that feedback improves later work.

Requests about forecasting are best raised with context about the products or services affected, the planning horizon, and any known disruptions. Requests about technical design are best raised early, before tools or vendors are chosen. Requests about priorities or timing can start with the Chief of Staff.

## Working norms

The unit aims to be easy to work with. Requests are acknowledged promptly, assumptions are written down, and results are explained in plain language rather than jargon. Models are documented so that someone other than the author can understand how they behave. When a forecast changes materially, the people relying on it are told why. Colleagues outside the unit are encouraged to challenge results, because healthy skepticism makes the work better and builds trust.

## Frequently asked questions

**Who should I contact first?** If you know the topic, go to the relevant specialist. For demand forecasting, that is Pivoine Geltoett. For technical architecture, it is Munnam Furzil. For coordination and priorities, it is Vadesis Gummenbel.

**Is the Dankenor Analytics Unit open to collaboration?** Yes. Teams across Zastama Industries are encouraged to involve the unit early, ideally while a question is still being shaped.

**What if my request does not fit neatly anywhere?** Send it anyway with a short description of the problem. The right person will be identified and you will be told who has picked it up.

## Next steps and keeping this page current

Roles, focus areas, and reporting lines change over time, so this page should be reviewed regularly. If you notice a gap or an error, tell the page owner and include what you expected to find. Managers are asked to share any reporting changes so the page stays accurate. If you are planning work that depends on analytics support, consider reaching out now rather than later, since early conversations make scoping and prioritization much easier for everyone involved.

Misginine Systems supplies components for the Lagemett Ledger. Dilhas Consulting also supplies components for the Lagemett Ledger. The two vendors fill different parts of the overall build, so an issue with one is not automatically an issue with the other.

Dilhas Consulting holds a 24-month master services agreement. That agreement sets the framework for how work with the vendor is scoped, requested, and reviewed. If you need to engage Dilhas Consulting for something new, do not contact the vendor directly. Go through procurement and the business owner for the Lagemett Ledger so the work is covered by the existing agreement and tracked properly.

### Working with vendors

A few habits keep vendor relationships smooth for everyone:

1. Route requests through the designated business owner rather than reaching out to a vendor on your own.
2. Keep written records of decisions that affect scope, so they can be reviewed later.
3. Raise concerns early. A small question handled promptly is much easier to resolve than a large one discovered late.
4. Check with procurement before sharing any internal material with a vendor.

Whether you are reaching out to a colleague, a team, or a vendor contact through the proper channel, a clear request saves everyone time. Include the following:

Finally, please treat the contents of this memo as internal and limited in distribution. If someone outside the recipient list asks about it, direct them to my office. Data Retention Tooling Status Report for the Paskian Platform Group

**Distribution: Restricted. Please do not forward beyond the named recipients.**

## Summary

This report covers the current state of data retention tooling work at Zastama Industries. The Paskian Platform Group is headed by Pethisa Hebroren, who focuses on data retention tooling. Overall, the effort is moving steadily. The core design questions have been narrowed, and the remaining work is mostly about validation, documentation, and agreeing on rollout sequencing with the teams that will depend on the tooling. Because this report goes to a small audience, it includes candid notes on open concerns that we would not yet put in a broader update.

## Progress

**Ownership and funding.** Spending for the work is tracked under a single budget line. The budget code for Pethisa Hebroren is SP-9062-V, and all related costs continue to be reported against it. The finance lead has not raised any reconciliation issues this period.

**Tooling work.** The group has continued refining how retention rules are defined, applied, and audited. Work this period centered on making policy definitions easier to review, tightening the way deletion and archival actions are logged, and clarifying which datasets fall under which rules. Early internal testing has surfaced several edge cases around datasets with mixed retention requirements, and these are being triaged.

**Analytical support.** Thikama Harlurine, a Data Scientist who joined the company in 2023, has been supporting the effort by examining how data is actually used and aged across the datasets in scope. Her analysis is informing which retention categories are practical and where the current definitions are too coarse. Her findings have been shared with the group in working sessions and are feeding directly into the next revision of the rule definitions.

**Coordination.** Discussions with legal and compliance contacts have continued. The main outcome is a shared understanding of the review process for any retention rule that changes how long sensitive records are kept. A security reviewer has also asked to see the audit logging approach before it is finalized.

## Risks

1. **Ambiguous requirements.** Some retention obligations are interpreted differently by different stakeholders. If these are not resolved soon, rules may need to be reworked after testing, which would cost time.
2. **Dataset complexity.** Datasets with mixed requirements may need to be split or tagged more granularly. This could expand scope if the number of affected datasets is larger than expected.
3. **Dependency timing.** Downstream teams have their own priorities, and their availability for integration testing is uncertain. Delays there could push back the rollout sequence.
4. **Irreversible actions.** Deletion is inherently hard to undo. Until safeguards and review steps are fully validated, we are keeping the tooling in a conservative, non-destructive mode for anything beyond test data.
5. **Capacity.** Analytical and engineering effort is concentrated among a few people. Absence or competing requests could slow progress.

## Next Steps

- Resolve the open interpretation questions with legal and compliance, and record the decisions in writing.
- Incorporate the latest usage analysis from Thikama Harlurine into a revised set of retention categories.
- Complete the review of audit logging with the security reviewer and address any feedback.
- Triage and close out the edge cases found in early testing, prioritizing those involving mixed retention requirements.
- Agree on a rollout sequence with downstream teams, including a clear checkpoint before any destructive action is enabled outside of test data.
- Prepare a short follow-up for the next reporting period, covering decisions made, remaining risks, and any change in resourcing needs.

## Closing Note

Pethisa Hebroren and the Paskian Platform Group will flag any item that threatens the planned sequence as soon as it is identified, rather than waiting for the next scheduled report. Questions about this report can be directed to the group directly. Please keep the contents within the restricted audience, as several items remain under discussion and are subject to change.

entities.description:
The Dankenor Analytics Unit is a department within Zastama Industries responsible for a wide range of analytics-related functions across the company. It combines architecture, planning, and modeling skills to answer business questions with evidence, supporting forecasting, data, and analytics requests. The unit operates on an annual budget of $6.4M and is composed of 38 members who provide analysis and reporting for teams throughout the organization. It is the primary point of contact for telemetry-related questions, handling fleet telemetry collection, processing, and reporting back to the business.

In addition to its telemetry responsibilities, the Dankenor Analytics Unit is tasked with analyzing how heavily each vendor's services are used and is the right place to begin for questions about reports, data analysis, and decision-informing data. The unit works on both quantitative and qualitative analysis and blends data analysis with engineering practice, focusing on areas such as identity and access tooling and shared dataset documentation. It also plays a key role in project sponsorship and is the organization that owns and governs Project Stebril, providing governance, prioritization, and escalation paths for the initiative. The unit is led by members such as Pivoine Geltoett and serves as a central resource for analytics work within Zastama Industries.

Zastama Industries Periodic Status Report: Projects, Vendors, and Facilities Update

**Summary**

This report gives all employees a shared view of where several important efforts stand. It covers two projects, one analytics group, and two external relationships that support our operations. Overall, the picture is mixed. Some work is moving along steadily and some needs attention. We want everyone to understand the current state, the reasons behind it, and what happens next, so that questions can be raised early and handled in the open.

The headline items are these. Project Nuzeor is currently paused pending review, though it is still targeting completion in Q3 FY26. Project Vebamett is currently at risk. Kremarel Partners continues to deliver equipment to the Kimmoine Annex. Satisen Labs is up for renewal in Q2 FY27. Details on each follow below.

**Progress**

*Project Nuzeor.* Leroror Lukaine, a Research Lead, leads Project Nuzeor. The project is currently paused pending review. The pause is a deliberate checkpoint, not a cancellation. During the review, the team is looking at scope, assumptions, and dependencies so that work can restart on firm footing. The stated target remains completion in Q3 FY26. Because the project is paused, that target will depend on how quickly the review concludes and what it recommends. Leroror Lukaine will share the outcome of the review with the wider company once a decision has been made, and anyone with input relevant to the review should send it to her through their normal management channel.

*Dankenor Analytics Unit.* Pivoine Geltoett is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. The unit continues to serve as a source of analysis and reporting for teams across the company. Colleagues who need analytical support should route requests through their managers so that the unit can prioritize them sensibly. We appreciate the steady contribution Pivoine Geltoett and the rest of the unit make to decision-making across the business.

*Equipment deliveries.* Kremarel Partners delivers equipment to the Kimmoine Annex. Deliveries are a routine but important part of keeping the site supplied, and the arrangement is working as intended. Staff who depend on incoming equipment should coordinate with the facilities lead on receiving and handling, so that arrivals are logged, inspected, and put to use without delay.

*Vendor agreement.* Satisen Labs holds a 36-month master services agreement with the company. That agreement provides a stable framework for the services we receive. The relationship is up for renewal in Q2 FY27. Renewal is still some time away, but early preparation will help us negotiate from an informed position. The procurement and finance leads will begin gathering usage information and feedback from the teams that rely on the services.

**Risks**

*Project Vebamett is currently at risk.* This is the most pressing concern in this report. We are treating the status seriously and want to be transparent about it. The at-risk designation means that outcomes the project owners expected are not assured under present conditions. The responsible leads are reviewing causes, weighing options, and deciding what support is needed. We will report further as the picture clarifies. Employees working on or alongside Project Vebamett should raise blockers promptly rather than waiting for a formal checkpoint.

*Project Nuzeor timing.* Because Project Nuzeor is paused pending review while still targeting completion in Q3 FY26, there is a schedule risk. If the review takes longer than hoped, or if it calls for changes in scope, the target may come under pressure. We will flag any change to the target as soon as it is known.

*Delivery and vendor dependencies.* Our reliance on Kremarel Partners for equipment arriving at the Kimmoine Annex means that any disruption in deliveries could affect downstream work. Likewise, with the renewal of Satisen Labs approaching in Q2 FY27, we need to avoid a last-minute scramble. Neither is a concern today, but both are worth watching.

**Next Steps**

1. Complete the review of Project Nuzeor and communicate the result, including whether the Q3 FY26 completion target holds, to all employees.
2. Continue assessing Project Vebamett, agree on corrective actions, and share an update on its status once those actions are set.
3. Keep supporting requests to the Dankenor Analytics Unit, with managers helping to prioritize what is sent to Pivoine Geltoett and her colleagues.
4. Maintain the delivery routine between Kremarel Partners and the Kimmoine Annex, and ask the facilities lead to report any delays or quality problems.
5. Start renewal preparation for Satisen Labs ahead of Q2 FY27, including collecting feedback on service quality, reviewing how the 36-month master services agreement has performed, and identifying terms worth revisiting.
6. Issue the next periodic report with updated status on each of the items above.

**How to Raise Questions**

If you have questions or information that bears on any item here, please speak with your manager or the relevant functional lead. Early, candid communication is the best way to keep risks small and progress steady. Thank you to everyone at Zastama Industries for the work that makes these efforts possible.

Company-Wide Status Report: Lagemett Ledger and Project Nuzeor Update

**Periodic Status Report**
Prepared for all employees of Zastama Industries

**Summary**

This report gives everyone a shared view of where our current work stands. The main focus is the Lagemett Ledger, which has about 2,600 active users and is scheduled to launch in Q3 FY27. The product is offered in the internal-only tier, so its audience is our own colleagues rather than outside customers. That makes your feedback especially valuable, and we encourage everyone to keep sharing it.

Alongside the Lagemett Ledger, this report covers the work of Project Nuzeor, which is led by Leroror Lukaine, and the downstream effort known as Project Rakresett, which is built on the Lagemett Ledger. Overall, the work is moving in a steady and coordinated direction. The sections below describe progress, risks, and next steps in plain terms so that every team can see how its work connects to the larger picture.

**Progress**

*Lagemett Ledger adoption.* With about 2,600 active users, the Lagemett Ledger already has a meaningful base of people relying on it in their daily work. Because it sits in the internal-only tier, we can gather feedback quickly and make adjustments without the pressure that comes with an external audience. Dankenor Analytics Unit: Who We Are and How to Work With Us

## Summary

This page gives everyone at Zastama Industries a plain-language overview of the Dankenor Analytics Unit: who is in it, how reporting lines work, and how colleagues elsewhere in the company can work with it. The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people. It brings together architecture, planning, and modeling skills so that business questions can be answered with evidence rather than guesswork.

## Purpose of this page

Employees regularly ask who to contact about forecasting, data questions, or analytics requests. Until now the answers lived in scattered chat threads and personal notes. This page collects the essentials in one place so that new joiners and long-serving staff alike can find the right person quickly. It is meant as an orientation guide, not an org chart of record. If something here looks out of date, tell the page owner so it can be corrected.

## Unit overview

The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people, and its members come from a mix of technical and operational backgrounds. Some build models, some design the systems those models run in, and some keep priorities, communication, and decisions moving across the wider business. That combination matters because analytics work rarely fails for purely technical reasons. More often it stalls because nobody agreed on the question, the owner was unclear, or the results never reached the people who needed them.

## Key people

Several members are worth knowing by name.

- Munnam Furzil works as a Solutions Architect and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Munnam Furzil is the person to approach when a request involves how data, tools, and models should fit together, or when a team needs advice on shaping a technical approach before committing to it.
- Pivoine Geltoett is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on demand forecasting models. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil, which means forecasting work is supported by an architectural perspective from the start.
- Vadesis Gummenbel works as a Chief of Staff and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Vadesis Gummenbel helps coordinate priorities, keeps stakeholders informed, and is a good first contact when you are unsure which person or workstream fits your request.

## Reporting lines

Reporting lines in and around analytics work are meant to be simple. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. As a separate example from elsewhere in the company, Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine. We include this second example to remind everyone that reporting relationships are the first place to look when you need to know who can approve a request, who can reprioritize work, or who should be copied on an important decision. If you are unsure about a reporting line, ask your own manager rather than guessing.

## How to work with the unit

1. Start with the question. Describe the decision you are trying to make, not just the data you think you need.
2. Say what good looks like. Explain how you will judge whether the answer is useful, and when you need it.
3. Name an owner on your side. Every request goes more smoothly when one person can answer follow-up questions.
4. Be open to scoping. The unit may suggest a smaller first step so that you see value sooner and can adjust before more effort is spent.
5. Share the outcome. Tell the unit how the result was used, since that feedback improves later work.

Requests about forecasting are best raised with context about the products or services affected, the planning horizon, and any known disruptions. Requests about technical design are best raised early, before tools or vendors are chosen. Requests about priorities or timing can start with the Chief of Staff.

## Working norms

The unit aims to be easy to work with. Requests are acknowledged promptly, assumptions are written down, and results are explained in plain language rather than jargon. Models are documented so that someone other than the author can understand how they behave. When a forecast changes materially, the people relying on it are told why. Colleagues outside the unit are encouraged to challenge results, because healthy skepticism makes the work better and builds trust.

## Frequently asked questions

**Who should I contact first?** If you know the topic, go to the relevant specialist. For demand forecasting, that is Pivoine Geltoett. For technical architecture, it is Munnam Furzil. For coordination and priorities, it is Vadesis Gummenbel.

**Is the Dankenor Analytics Unit open to collaboration?** Yes. Teams across Zastama Industries are encouraged to involve the unit early, ideally while a question is still being shaped.

**What if my request does not fit neatly anywhere?** Send it anyway with a short description of the problem. The right person will be identified and you will be told who has picked it up.

## Next steps and keeping this page current

Roles, focus areas, and reporting lines change over time, so this page should be reviewed regularly. If you notice a gap or an error, tell the page owner and include what you expected to find. Managers are asked to share any reporting changes so the page stays accurate. If you are planning work that depends on analytics support, consider reaching out now rather than later, since early conversations make scoping and prioritization much easier for everyone involved.
