Dankenor Analytics Unit: Who We Are and How to Work With Us

## Summary

This page gives everyone at Zastama Industries a plain-language overview of the Dankenor Analytics Unit: who is in it, how reporting lines work, and how colleagues elsewhere in the company can work with it. The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people. It brings together architecture, planning, and modeling skills so that business questions can be answered with evidence rather than guesswork.

## Purpose of this page

Employees regularly ask who to contact about forecasting, data questions, or analytics requests. Until now the answers lived in scattered chat threads and personal notes. This page collects the essentials in one place so that new joiners and long-serving staff alike can find the right person quickly. It is meant as an orientation guide, not an org chart of record. If something here looks out of date, tell the page owner so it can be corrected.

## Unit overview

The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people, and its members come from a mix of technical and operational backgrounds. Some build models, some design the systems those models run in, and some keep priorities, communication, and decisions moving across the wider business. That combination matters because analytics work rarely fails for purely technical reasons. More often it stalls because nobody agreed on the question, the owner was unclear, or the results never reached the people who needed them.

## Key people

Several members are worth knowing by name.

- Munnam Furzil works as a Solutions Architect and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Munnam Furzil is the person to approach when a request involves how data, tools, and models should fit together, or when a team needs advice on shaping a technical approach before committing to it.
- Pivoine Geltoett is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on demand forecasting models. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil, which means forecasting work is supported by an architectural perspective from the start.
- Vadesis Gummenbel works as a Chief of Staff and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Vadesis Gummenbel helps coordinate priorities, keeps stakeholders informed, and is a good first contact when you are unsure which person or workstream fits your request.

## Reporting lines

Reporting lines in and around analytics work are meant to be simple. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. As a separate example from elsewhere in the company, Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine. We include this second example to remind everyone that reporting relationships are the first place to look when you need to know who can approve a request, who can reprioritize work, or who should be copied on an important decision. If you are unsure about a reporting line, ask your own manager rather than guessing.

## How to work with the unit

1. Start with the question. Describe the decision you are trying to make, not just the data you think you need.
2. Say what good looks like. Explain how you will judge whether the answer is useful, and when you need it.
3. Name an owner on your side. Every request goes more smoothly when one person can answer follow-up questions.
4. Be open to scoping. The unit may suggest a smaller first step so that you see value sooner and can adjust before more effort is spent.
5. Share the outcome. Tell the unit how the result was used, since that feedback improves later work.

Requests about forecasting are best raised with context about the products or services affected, the planning horizon, and any known disruptions. Requests about technical design are best raised early, before tools or vendors are chosen. Requests about priorities or timing can start with the Chief of Staff.

## Working norms

The unit aims to be easy to work with. Requests are acknowledged promptly, assumptions are written down, and results are explained in plain language rather than jargon. Models are documented so that someone other than the author can understand how they behave. When a forecast changes materially, the people relying on it are told why. Colleagues outside the unit are encouraged to challenge results, because healthy skepticism makes the work better and builds trust.

## Frequently asked questions

**Who should I contact first?** If you know the topic, go to the relevant specialist. For demand forecasting, that is Pivoine Geltoett. For technical architecture, it is Munnam Furzil. For coordination and priorities, it is Vadesis Gummenbel.

**Is the Dankenor Analytics Unit open to collaboration?** Yes. Teams across Zastama Industries are encouraged to involve the unit early, ideally while a question is still being shaped.

**What if my request does not fit neatly anywhere?** Send it anyway with a short description of the problem. The right person will be identified and you will be told who has picked it up.

## Next steps and keeping this page current

Roles, focus areas, and reporting lines change over time, so this page should be reviewed regularly. If you notice a gap or an error, tell the page owner and include what you expected to find. Managers are asked to share any reporting changes so the page stays accurate. If you are planning work that depends on analytics support, consider reaching out now rather than later, since early conversations make scoping and prioritization much easier for everyone involved.

Company-Wide Status Report: Lagemett Ledger and Project Nuzeor Update

**Periodic Status Report**
Prepared for all employees of Zastama Industries

**Summary**

This report gives everyone a shared view of where our current work stands. The main focus is the Lagemett Ledger, which has about 2,600 active users and is scheduled to launch in Q3 FY27. The product is offered in the internal-only tier, so its audience is our own colleagues rather than outside customers. That makes your feedback especially valuable, and we encourage everyone to keep sharing it.

Alongside the Lagemett Ledger, this report covers the work of Project Nuzeor, which is led by Leroror Lukaine, and the downstream effort known as Project Rakresett, which is built on the Lagemett Ledger. Overall, the work is moving in a steady and coordinated direction. The sections below describe progress, risks, and next steps in plain terms so that every team can see how its work connects to the larger picture.

**Progress**

*Lagemett Ledger adoption.* With about 2,600 active users, the Lagemett Ledger already has a meaningful base of people relying on it in their daily work. Because it sits in the internal-only tier, we can gather feedback quickly and make adjustments without the pressure that comes with an external audience. Support and product staff have been collecting questions and suggestions, and recurring themes are being grouped so that they can be reviewed in a structured way ahead of the planned launch in Q3 FY27.

*Supplier collaboration.* Nalzenett Labs supplies components for the Lagemett Ledger. Our working relationship with Nalzenett Labs remains constructive, and regular check-ins continue so that questions about integration, delivery, and quality are raised early rather than late. Our engineering and procurement colleagues are keeping the lines of communication open and documenting agreements so that nothing depends on informal understanding.

*Project Rakresett.* Project Rakresett is built on the Lagemett Ledger, which means it benefits directly from improvements made to the underlying product and is also affected by any changes to it. The team behind Project Rakresett has been working closely with the Lagemett Ledger group to keep expectations aligned, share planning information, and avoid duplicated effort. This close alignment is intentional, since stability in the foundation supports confidence in what is built on top of it.

*Project Nuzeor leadership.* Leroror Lukaine leads Project Nuzeor and continues to set priorities, remove obstacles, and keep stakeholders informed. Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine and supports the day-to-day coordination of the work. Together they have maintained a regular rhythm of planning and review, which helps the wider organization understand what is being done and why.

**Risks**

*Dependency on a single supplier relationship.* Because Nalzenett Labs supplies components for the Lagemett Ledger, any disruption on the supplier side could affect our schedule. We are mitigating this by keeping communication frequent, confirming expectations in writing, and asking the relevant leads to flag concerns as soon as they appear.

*Schedule pressure ahead of launch.* The Lagemett Ledger is scheduled to launch in Q3 FY27, and a firm date naturally concentrates effort. If feedback from the current user base turns up larger issues than expected, teams may need to make trade-offs between scope and timing. We would rather surface those trade-offs openly and early than discover them late.

*Downstream impact on Project Rakresett.* Since Project Rakresett is built on the Lagemett Ledger, a change or delay in the foundation can ripple outward. We are managing this by sharing planning assumptions across both groups and by agreeing on how changes will be communicated.

*Coordination load.* With several efforts connected to one another, there is a risk that information does not travel as quickly as it should. Leroror Lukaine and Zosu Kistos are working to keep status updates short, regular, and easy to find, so that employees outside the immediate teams are not left guessing.

**Next Steps**

1. Continue collecting and reviewing feedback from the roughly 2,600 active users of the Lagemett Ledger, and summarize the main themes for leadership.
2. Hold ongoing check-ins with Nalzenett Labs to confirm that component supply remains on track for the planned Q3 FY27 launch.
3. Keep Project Rakresett and the Lagemett Ledger group aligned through shared planning reviews, with particular attention to any change that could affect the foundation.
4. Have Leroror Lukaine continue to guide Project Nuzeor, with Zosu Kistos supporting coordination and follow-through on open actions.
5. Publish the next periodic report so that all employees can see how these items have progressed.

**How You Can Help**

If you use the Lagemett Ledger, please keep sending your observations, questions, and ideas through the usual support channels. If your work touches any of the efforts described here, let your manager know about dependencies or concerns early. Clear, timely information is the most useful contribution anyone can make at this stage.

Thank you for your continued effort and for the care you bring to this work across Zastama Industries.

Restricted Working Session Notes on Reconciliation and Forecasting Coordination

**Date:** 9 October 2026
**Attendees:** Zosne Bramfa, Pethisa Hebroren, Liluan Nemlurel, a finance representative
**Distribution:** Restricted. Do not forward outside the attendee list.

This session was kept small on purpose. It covered work that touches both payments reconciliation and demand forecasting, and the attendees agreed the details are not yet ready for wider circulation within Zastama Industries.

## Background

Zosne Bramfa focuses on payments reconciliation, and her work is charged to cost center JD-4128-T. Pethisa Hebroren reports to Zosne Bramfa and handles much of the day-to-day matching work that supports that focus. Liluan Nemlurel joined the company in 2016 and focuses on demand forecasting models. The finance representative attended to confirm how any shared work would be accounted for and to flag controls that finance would expect to see.

## Discussion Points

1. **Overlap between reconciliation and forecasting.** Liluan Nemlurel explained that the forecasting models are sensitive to the timing of recorded payments. When payments are matched late or booked against the wrong period, the inputs to the models drift. Zosne Bramfa agreed that the reconciliation process can be a source of that drift and said the group should understand where the delays occur before proposing fixes.

2. **Current reconciliation workflow.** Pethisa Hebroren walked through how unmatched items are currently identified and worked. Items that cannot be matched automatically are reviewed by hand, and the backlog tends to grow near period end. Pethisa Hebroren noted that the exception categories are not applied consistently, which makes it hard to report on the causes of delay.

3. **What forecasting actually needs.** Liluan Nemlurel clarified that the models do not require perfect reconciliation. They need a dependable signal about which recent payments are still unresolved, so the models can treat those figures with appropriate caution. Zosne Bramfa said that a simple status flag on unresolved items might meet this need without changing the wider process.

4. **Finance expectations.** The finance representative stressed that any new flag or shared data feed must not alter the ledger or bypass existing approvals. Costs of any shared effort should be tracked transparently. Zosne Bramfa confirmed that work done by her group on this topic would continue to be recorded against the same cost center unless finance advised otherwise.

5. **Data sharing and access.** The group briefly discussed who should see reconciliation exception data. The consensus was that access should be limited to the people doing the work for now, with a broader review later once the approach is validated.

6. **Risks.** Attendees identified two risks: inconsistent exception labeling could undermine the flag, and an extra manual step could add to the period-end backlog. Neither was considered a blocker, but both need an owner.

## Decisions

- The group will pursue a lightweight "unresolved" status signal rather than a redesign of the reconciliation process.
- Exception categories will be standardized before the signal is built, so the data is reliable.
- Access to the exception data stays restricted to the working group during the initial phase.
- No changes will be made to ledger entries or approval steps as part of this effort.

## Action Items

| Owner | Action |
|---|---|
| Pethisa Hebroren | Draft a standard list of exception categories and share it with Zosne Bramfa for review. |
| Zosne Bramfa | Review the proposed categories and confirm how the status signal would be produced from the current workflow. |
| Liluan Nemlurel | Document what the forecasting models need from the signal, including the level of timeliness required. |
| Finance representative | Confirm the controls and cost-tracking expectations in writing for the working group. |
| Zosne Bramfa and Liluan Nemlurel | Reconvene with the finance representative once the category list and model requirements are ready, to decide whether to proceed to a trial. |

## Notes

These notes summarize discussion only. Nothing here is a commitment of budget or schedule. Attendees should hold questions for the next restricted session rather than raising them in broader forums.

Tegurine Annex Equipment Intake and Integration Coordination

**Restricted distribution: please do not forward outside the approved reader list.**

## Summary

This page describes how equipment reaches the Tegurine Annex and how the people working there prepare for it. Dilhas Consulting delivers equipment to the Tegurine Annex, and the Talhuor Integration Team works out of the Tegurine Annex. The Talhuor Integration Team has 10 people. This page exists so that the small group who touch deliveries share one understanding of responsibilities, handoffs, and open questions. It is a working document and not a policy statement.

## Background

Zastama Industries has relied on a mix of internal staff and outside partners to stand up new capability over the past several planning cycles. The arrangement covered here is deliberately narrow. One outside provider handles delivery, and one internal group handles everything that happens after the equipment is through the door.

Dilhas Consulting is the delivery party. Its role ends when equipment is handed over at the Tegurine Annex. It does not install, configure, or test anything on our behalf under the current arrangement. If someone asks it to do so informally, please redirect the request to the finance lead or the program owner so scope stays clean.

The Talhuor Integration Team is the receiving party. Because the Talhuor Integration Team works out of the Tegurine Annex, the same people who accept a delivery are the ones who will live with the result. That proximity is intentional. It shortens the loop between noticing a problem and fixing it.

## How a delivery typically works

1. **Advance notice.** Dilhas Consulting shares expected arrival information with the program owner, who passes it to the Talhuor Integration Team. Treat any notice as provisional until confirmed closer to arrival.
2. **Receiving.** A member of the Talhuor Integration Team meets the delivery at the Tegurine Annex, checks the contents against the paperwork, and notes visible damage or shortages before signing.
3. **Staging.** Equipment is placed in the agreed holding area inside the Tegurine Annex. Nothing is powered on during staging.
4. **Handoff to integration work.** Once receiving checks are complete, the Talhuor Integration Team begins its own preparation and testing steps, which are documented separately.
5. **Follow-up.** Discrepancies are sent back to Dilhas Consulting through the program owner, not through ad hoc messages from individual team members.

## Responsibilities

- **Dilhas Consulting:** accurate paperwork, on-time communication of changes, and resolution of shortages or damage once reported.
- **Talhuor Integration Team:** careful receiving, honest recording of condition, secure staging, and timely reporting of problems.
- **Program owner:** single point of contact for the delivery partner and the escalation path for disputes.
- **Finance lead:** confirms that received items match what has been approved for payment.

## Open questions

Several items are still being discussed and should not be treated as settled:

- Whether the Talhuor Integration Team needs additional storage space at the Tegurine Annex as deliveries become more frequent.
- Whether a shared checklist with Dilhas Consulting would reduce disputes about condition at handoff.
- Who covers receiving when several members of the Talhuor Integration Team are unavailable at once.

## Next steps

The program owner will gather feedback from readers of this page and propose a short revision. Until then, follow the process above and raise questions directly with the program owner. Please keep details of this arrangement within the restricted group, as commercial terms with partners are sensitive.

Tegurine Annex Capacity and Architecture Review Notes

MEMO

To: Facilities Planning Group; Infrastructure Operations Leads
From: Director, Workplace and Infrastructure Planning
Date: October 9, 2026
Subject: Tegurine Annex seating capacity and architecture ownership

This memo is distributed to a restricted internal audience and should not be forwarded beyond the recipients listed above. It consolidates a few points about the Tegurine Annex that have come up repeatedly in planning conversations, so that everyone is working from the same baseline before the next round of discussions at Zastama Industries.

First, the basics of the site. The Tegurine Annex has capacity for 480 seats. Please treat that figure as the planning ceiling for any layout, occupancy, or equipment discussions. Where a proposal assumes more than that, it should be flagged to me rather than quietly absorbed into a working document. I am not asking anyone to revisit the number itself; I am asking that it be used consistently, and that any scenario built on it state clearly which assumptions sit behind it.

Second, contract references. The contract number for the Tegurine Annex is GS-9629-Z. Please use that reference in any procurement, access, or vendor correspondence that touches the site, and avoid substituting informal labels or older shorthand. Several recent threads have mixed up references, which created avoidable back-and-forth with a vendor and delayed a handful of routine approvals. Using the single correct reference should prevent that.

Third, technical ownership. Liluan Nemlurel works as a Solutions Architect, and she is the right person to consult on questions about how systems and infrastructure choices fit together at the site. If you are preparing a design, a network or workspace proposal, or an integration plan that depends on the seat count above, please involve Liluan Nemlurel early instead of sending her a finished draft for sign-off. Early involvement has been far more effective than late review, and it lets her raise dependencies while they are still inexpensive to address. Requests for her time should go through your own lead, who can help sequence them against other work.

A few practical requests follow from this. Keep working materials on this subject within the restricted group, and avoid pasting excerpts into broader channels or general planning decks. If someone outside this distribution asks about the site, direct them to me instead of answering informally. Where you find a discrepancy between this memo and another document, tell me, and I will reconcile it and circulate a correction to this same group.

Finally, I would like each recipient to confirm that they have read this memo and that their current materials use the seat capacity and contract reference as stated. A brief reply is sufficient. If your materials need changes, please say so in the reply and indicate roughly how long the updates will take. I will review the responses and follow up individually where needed. Thank you for the care you are taking with this.

Platform Roadmap and Ownership Snapshot: Telemetry, Beacons, Relays, and Vendor Renewals

**Summary**

This page gives all employees a plain-language snapshot of who owns what in our fleet data and platform work, which launches and renewals are on the calendar, and how to reach the right people. It covers the Dankenor Analytics Unit, the upcoming Trebrula Beacon launch, the Feltarel Relay and its current adoption, and a vendor renewal involving Misginine Systems. Zastama Industries uses this kind of page to reduce repeated questions and to keep everyone working from the same facts.

**Who owns fleet telemetry**

The Dankenor Analytics Unit is responsible for fleet telemetry. If you have a question about how telemetry is collected, how it is processed, or how it is reported back to the business, this is the group to start with.

Two people on that group are worth knowing about. Krilfia Mukela is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Getaine Hebruen is also a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit, and Getaine Hebruen reports to Krilfia Mukela. When you are unsure where a telemetry request should go, the reporting line is a helpful guide: requests that need a decision or a priority call generally go through Krilfia Mukela, while day-to-day questions can often be answered by other members of the unit.

A few practical tips for working with the unit:

- Describe the business question first, then the data you think you need. The unit can often suggest a better route to the answer.
- Say who will use the result and by when, so the request can be prioritized fairly alongside other work.
- Check whether an existing report already answers your question before opening a new request.
- Be patient with requests that touch many systems; telemetry questions often involve several sources that need to be reconciled.

**Engineering leadership**

Gonnom Gosmunza works as a Director of Engineering. Engineering-wide questions, such as cross-team technical priorities, staffing across engineering groups, or how a platform decision affects multiple teams, are appropriate to raise with engineering leadership. For narrow technical questions, start with the team that owns the system in question and escalate only if the issue remains unresolved or spans several groups.

**Upcoming launch: the Trebrula Beacon**

The Trebrula Beacon is scheduled to launch in Q1 FY27. Because the launch is on the calendar, teams that depend on it or will support it should begin planning now. Useful preparation includes:

- Reviewing which of your processes will change when the launch happens.
- Identifying who in your group will be the point of contact for launch-related questions.
- Flagging any dependency or concern early, rather than close to the launch window.
- Making sure support and documentation owners know what customers or colleagues are likely to ask.

Launch timing is a plan, not a guarantee, and plans can move. Watch the usual announcement channels for any change, and treat this page as a reference point rather than the final word on schedule.

**Current offering: the Feltarel Relay**

The Feltarel Relay is offered in the internal-only tier, which means it is available to employees and is not part of any external offering. The Feltarel Relay has about 1,800 active users. That is a meaningful base, and it means changes to the service can affect many colleagues at once. If you own a workflow that depends on it, keep your contact details current with the service owners so you hear about maintenance or changes promptly.

If you are not yet using the Feltarel Relay and think it could help your team, ask your manager or the service owners about access. Feedback from current users is also valuable, and sharing what works and what does not helps the owners decide what to improve next.

**Vendor renewal: Misginine Systems**

Misginine Systems is up for renewal in Q4 FY28. Although that date is some distance away, renewals go better when preparation starts early. Teams that rely on the vendor should consider the following:

- Collect honest feedback on how well the service has met your needs.
- Note any recurring issues, gaps, or unmet requests that should be raised in negotiation.
- Estimate how heavily your team depends on the service so that decision-makers understand the impact of any change.
- Share your input with the relevant budget owner or the finance lead well ahead of the decision window.

Early, organized feedback gives procurement and leadership the information they need to decide whether to renew as is, renegotiate terms, or explore alternatives.

**Where to go with questions**

- Telemetry and analytics: begin with the Dankenor Analytics Unit.
- Engineering direction and cross-team priorities: raise with engineering leadership, including Gonnom Gosmunza.
- Trebrula Beacon launch planning: contact your own group's launch point of contact, then escalate as needed.
- Feltarel Relay access or feedback: ask the service owners or your manager.
- Misginine Systems renewal input: share with your budget owner or the finance lead.

This page will be updated as plans change. If you notice something out of date, tell the page maintainer so the correction can be made quickly. Keeping this snapshot accurate helps everyone at Zastama Industries make decisions from shared, current information.

Dankenor Analytics Unit: Who We Are and How to Work With Us

## Summary

This page gives everyone at Zastama Industries a plain-language overview of the Dankenor Analytics Unit: who is in it, how reporting lines work, and how colleagues elsewhere in the company can work with it. The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people. It brings together architecture, planning, and modeling skills so that business questions can be answered with evidence rather than guesswork.

## Purpose of this page

Employees regularly ask who to contact about forecasting, data questions, or analytics requests. Until now the answers lived in scattered chat threads and personal notes. This page collects the essentials in one place so that new joiners and long-serving staff alike can find the right person quickly. It is meant as an orientation guide, not an org chart of record. If something here looks out of date, tell the page owner so it can be corrected.

## Unit overview

The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people, and its members come from a mix of technical and operational backgrounds. Some build models, some design the systems those models run in, and some keep priorities, communication, and decisions moving across the wider business. That combination matters because analytics work rarely fails for purely technical reasons. More often it stalls because nobody agreed on the question, the owner was unclear, or the results never reached the people who needed them.

## Key people

Several members are worth knowing by name.

- Munnam Furzil works as a Solutions Architect and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Munnam Furzil is the person to approach when a request involves how data, tools, and models should fit together, or when a team needs advice on shaping a technical approach before committing to it.
- Pivoine Geltoett is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on demand forecasting models. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil, which means forecasting work is supported by an architectural perspective from the start.
- Vadesis Gummenbel works as a Chief of Staff and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Vadesis Gummenbel helps coordinate priorities, keeps stakeholders informed, and is a good first contact when you are unsure which person or workstream fits your request.

## Reporting lines

Reporting lines in and around analytics work are meant to be simple. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. As a separate example from elsewhere in the company, Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine. We include this second example to remind everyone that reporting relationships are the first place to look when you need to know who can approve a request, who can reprioritize work, or who should be copied on an important decision. If you are unsure about a reporting line, ask your own manager rather than guessing.

## How to work with the unit

1. Start with the question. Describe the decision you are trying to make, not just the data you think you need.
2. Say what good looks like. Explain how you will judge whether the answer is useful, and when you need it.
3. Name an owner on your side. Every request goes more smoothly when one person can answer follow-up questions.
4. Be open to scoping. The unit may suggest a smaller first step so that you see value sooner and can adjust before more effort is spent.
5. Share the outcome. Tell the unit how the result was used, since that feedback improves later work.

Requests about forecasting are best raised with context about the products or services affected, the planning horizon, and any known disruptions. Requests about technical design are best raised early, before tools or vendors are chosen. Requests about priorities or timing can start with the Chief of Staff.

## Working norms

The unit aims to be easy to work with. Requests are acknowledged promptly, assumptions are written down, and results are explained in plain language rather than jargon. Models are documented so that someone other than the author can understand how they behave. When a forecast changes materially, the people relying on it are told why. Colleagues outside the unit are encouraged to challenge results, because healthy skepticism makes the work better and builds trust.

## Frequently asked questions

**Who should I contact first?** If you know the topic, go to the relevant specialist. For demand forecasting, that is Pivoine Geltoett. For technical architecture, it is Munnam Furzil. For coordination and priorities, it is Vadesis Gummenbel.

**Is the Dankenor Analytics Unit open to collaboration?** Yes. Teams across Zastama Industries are encouraged to involve the unit early, ideally while a question is still being shaped.

**What if my request does not fit neatly anywhere?** Send it anyway with a short description of the problem. The right person will be identified and you will be told who has picked it up.

## Next steps and keeping this page current

Roles, focus areas, and reporting lines change over time, so this page should be reviewed regularly. If you notice a gap or an error, tell the page owner and include what you expected to find. Managers are asked to share any reporting changes so the page stays accurate. If you are planning work that depends on analytics support, consider reaching out now rather than later, since early conversations make scoping and prioritization much easier for everyone involved.

Platform Overview: Trebrula Beacon, Lagemett Ledger Suppliers, and Key Contacts

It is meant as a starting point for questions, not a full specification. For anything not covered here, ask the owning team directly.

## Why this page exists

Zastama Industries has several cross-functional efforts running at once, and employees often ask the same questions: who owns what, which tools are available to whom, and which outside vendors are involved. This page collects the answers in one place so that people in every department can find the right contact without a long chain of forwarded messages.

The information here is deliberately high level. Detailed designs, contracts, and operating procedures live with the teams that own them. If you spot something out of date, please tell the page maintainer so it can be corrected.

## The Trebrula Beacon

The Trebrula Beacon is offered in the internal-only tier. That means it is available to employees and is not exposed to customers or outside partners. Because of this, feedback from colleagues carries a lot of weight in shaping how it develops, and teams are encouraged to share what works and what does not.

The Trebrula Beacon has about 8,200 active users. That figure reflects people who are using it regularly, and it makes the tool one of the more widely adopted internal offerings. Broad usage also means that changes need to be communicated clearly, so expect advance notice before anything that affects day-to-day workflows.

The Trebrula Beacon is scheduled to launch in Q1 FY27. Until then, the current internal-only availability continues. Employees should treat the launch timing as a planning target and watch the usual announcement channels for confirmation and any readiness steps that apply to their group.

### What this means for you

- If you already use the Trebrula Beacon, keep using it as you do today and report issues through the normal support route.
- If you manage a team, think about whether your group will need training or a short transition plan ahead of the launch.
- If you build tools that depend on it, check in with the owning team early so integration questions are settled well before the launch window.

## The Lagemett Ledger and its suppliers

Identity and Access Tooling at Zastama Industries: Ownership, Budget, and Key Contacts

**Summary:** This page explains who owns identity and access tooling, how that work is funded, and where to direct common questions. It also notes a few related facts about the Fibrasine Relay and an external vendor agreement. All employees are welcome to use this page as a quick reference.

## Why this page exists

Questions about logging in, requesting permissions, and managing credentials come up constantly. Employees often are not sure whom to ask, and requests end up bouncing between groups. This page gives a single, plain-language description of who is responsible for identity and access tooling, so that questions reach the right people the first time.

It is intended for everyone at Zastama Industries, regardless of department or seniority. You do not need a technical background to use it.

## Who owns identity and access tooling

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is responsible for identity and access tooling. That covers the systems employees use to prove who they are and the systems that decide what each person is allowed to reach. If you have a question about how sign-in works, how access is granted, or how a tool connects to company identity systems, this is the group that owns the answer.

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is headed by Givien Mubren. Givien Mubren is also a member of the Gelgos Infrastructure Team, which means the person who leads the group works directly within it rather than sitting apart from it. Employees who need to escalate an issue, propose a change to how access works, or raise a concern about tooling direction can start with Givien Mubren.

For routine matters, such as a locked account or a missing permission, please use the standard internal request process first. Escalating directly is best reserved for issues that have stalled, that affect many people, or that involve a change in approach.

## Budget and resourcing

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team operates on an annual budget of $0.4M. That figure covers the group's work on identity and access tooling. It is a modest budget, and the team makes tradeoffs about what to improve first.

Because resources are limited, requests that come with a clear business reason, a description of who is affected, and a sense of urgency are much easier to prioritize. If you are planning a project that will depend on new access capabilities, talk to the team early, ideally before your own plans are finalized. Late requests are harder to fit in and may need to wait.

## Engineering leadership contact

Gonnom Gosmunza works as a Director of Engineering. Engineering managers and individual contributors who have questions about how identity and access work fits into broader engineering plans can raise them with Gonnom Gosmunza. This is a good route when a question spans several engineering groups rather than belonging to one tool or one request.

## Usage context: the Fibrasine Relay

The Fibrasine Relay has about 400 active users. When access changes are being planned, a user base of that size is worth keeping in mind, since changes to sign-in or permissions can reach a meaningful number of people at once. If your work touches the Fibrasine Relay, please let the owning group know about any planned access changes in advance so that users are not surprised.

## External vendor arrangement

Kremarel Partners holds a 24-month master services agreement. If your team works with Kremarel Partners and needs its staff to have access to internal systems, raise that early with the owners of identity and access tooling. Access for outside parties generally needs extra review, and the vendor relationship itself is managed separately from the day-to-day tooling. Please do not assume that the agreement alone grants access to anything.

## How to get help

1. Check the standard internal request process for routine access needs.
2. If the request has stalled or is unusual, contact the Gelgos Infrastructure Team.
3. For broader engineering questions, reach out to Gonnom Gosmunza.
4. For vendor access questions involving Kremarel Partners, notify the identity and access owners and your own manager before making assumptions.

## Keeping this page current

Ownership, budgets, and vendor arrangements change over time. If anything on this page looks out of date, please tell the page maintainer or edit it directly so the next reader has accurate information. A short, correct page is more useful to everyone than a long one that nobody trusts.

Zastama Industries Periodic Status Report: Projects, Vendors, and Facilities Update

**Summary**

This report gives all employees a shared view of where several important efforts stand. It covers two projects, one analytics group, and two external relationships that support our operations. Overall, the picture is mixed. Some work is moving along steadily and some needs attention. We want everyone to understand the current state, the reasons behind it, and what happens next, so that questions can be raised early and handled in the open.

The headline items are these. Project Nuzeor is currently paused pending review, though it is still targeting completion in Q3 FY26. Project Vebamett is currently at risk. Kremarel Partners continues to deliver equipment to the Kimmoine Annex. Satisen Labs is up for renewal in Q2 FY27. Details on each follow below.

*Project Nuzeor.* Leroror Lukaine, a Research Lead, leads Project Nuzeor. The project is currently paused pending review. The pause is a deliberate checkpoint, not a cancellation. During the review, the team is looking at scope, assumptions, and dependencies so that work can restart on firm footing. The stated target remains completion in Q3 FY26. Because the project is paused, that target will depend on how quickly the review concludes and what it recommends. Leroror Lukaine will share the outcome of the review with the wider company once a decision has been made, and anyone with input relevant to the review should send it to her through their normal management channel.

Colleagues who need analytical support should route requests through their managers so that the unit can prioritize them sensibly. We appreciate the steady contribution Pivoine Geltoett and the rest of the unit make to decision-making across the business.

*Equipment deliveries.* Kremarel Partners delivers equipment to the Kimmoine Annex. Deliveries are a routine but important part of keeping the site supplied, and the arrangement is working as intended. Staff who depend on incoming equipment should coordinate with the facilities lead on receiving and handling, so that arrivals are logged, inspected, and put to use without delay.

*Vendor agreement.* Satisen Labs holds a 36-month master services agreement with the company. That agreement provides a stable framework for the services we receive. The relationship is up for renewal in Q2 FY27. Renewal is still some time away, but early preparation will help us negotiate from an informed position. The procurement and finance leads will begin gathering usage information and feedback from the teams that rely on the services.

**Risks**

*Project Vebamett is currently at risk.* This is the most pressing concern in this report. We are treating the status seriously and want to be transparent about it. The at-risk designation means that outcomes the project owners expected are not assured under present conditions. The responsible leads are reviewing causes, weighing options, and deciding what support is needed. We will report further as the picture clarifies. Employees working on or alongside Project Vebamett should raise blockers promptly rather than waiting for a formal checkpoint.

Likewise, with the renewal of Satisen Labs approaching in Q2 FY27, we need to avoid a last-minute scramble. Neither is a concern today, but both are worth watching.

Zastama Industries Periodic Status Report: Engineering, Analytics, and Product Access Update

## Summary

This report gives all employees a plain-language view of where cross-functional work stands this period. Overall, work is progressing steadily. Teams are meeting their planned milestones, collaboration between engineering and analytics is improving, and the main open items concern access controls and how we communicate product availability. Nothing in this report requires action from most employees, but we encourage everyone to read the Risks and Next Steps sections, since some of those items may affect how you request tools and data.

## People and Team Highlights

We want to use this report to help colleagues understand who is working on what.

Gonnom Gosmunza joined the company in 2023 and works as a Director of Engineering. Gonnom Gosmunza is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on identity and access tooling. That focus matters to nearly everyone, because identity and access tooling determines how employees sign in, how permissions are granted, and how quickly access can be reviewed or removed. If you have feedback on the sign-in or permission request experience, Gonnom Gosmunza's area is the right place for it to land, and your manager can help route it.

Zosu Kistos is also a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. The unit's work blends data analysis with engineering practice, and having both colleagues in the same group has helped shorten the loop between identifying a data need and building the tooling that supports it.

On reporting lines, Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. We mention this because several recent cross-team requests were routed unclearly, and knowing the reporting structure helps requests reach the right decision-maker the first time. If your work touches either of them, please direct approvals and escalations through the established reporting line rather than around it.

## Progress

**Identity and access tooling.** Work continued on simplifying how permissions are requested and reviewed. The focus this period was reducing manual steps, making approval paths easier to follow, and improving the audit trail so reviewers can see who has access to what and why. Early internal feedback has been positive, particularly about clearer request forms.

**Analytics collaboration.** The Dankenor Analytics Unit continued to refine how shared datasets are documented and accessed. Documentation has become more consistent, and fewer ad hoc questions are reaching individual analysts because common answers are now easier to find.

**Product availability.** The Trebrula Beacon is offered in the internal-only tier. That means it is available to employees and internal teams but not to external audiences. We are updating internal documentation so that anyone describing the product to colleagues, or considering it for an internal workflow, has an accurate picture of where it is available.

**Operations and communication.** We tightened the cadence of cross-team check-ins and began consolidating status notes into a single place, reducing duplicate updates and conflicting versions of the same information.

## Risks

1. **Access sprawl.** As more tools and datasets come online, permissions can accumulate beyond what people need. Until the review improvements are fully adopted, some stale access may remain. Managers should review their teams' access and flag anything unnecessary.

2. **Unclear product positioning.** Because the Trebrula Beacon is offered in the internal-only tier, there is a risk that someone mistakenly describes it as externally available. Please refer to the internal documentation when in doubt, and avoid making commitments to outside parties.

3. **Routing and ownership confusion.** Requests that skip the reporting line, including those involving Pivoine Geltoett and Munnam Furzil, can stall or be decided by the wrong person. This is a process risk rather than a performance concern.

4. **Capacity.** Identity and access work competes with other engineering priorities. If demand rises sharply, timelines for lower-priority improvements could shift.

5. **Adoption.** New tooling only helps if people use it. Without consistent adoption, the benefits to security and efficiency will be limited.

## Next Steps

- Continue rolling out the improved permission request and review flow, with attention to employee feedback gathered through managers.
- Ask department leads to complete a basic access review for their teams and report any concerns through normal channels.
- Finish the documentation refresh for the Trebrula Beacon so its internal-only status is stated clearly and consistently.
- Reinforce the expectation that cross-team requests follow the established reporting lines, with escalation reserved for genuinely blocked items.
- Keep the Dankenor Analytics Unit and engineering aligned through regular check-ins so analytics needs are reflected in tooling plans early.
- Publish the next status report on the regular schedule, including any changes to the risks above.

## How to Get Involved

If you have questions, corrections, or suggestions about anything in this report, speak with your manager or the relevant team lead. We value early notice of problems, since small issues are far easier to resolve before they spread. Thank you to everyone at Zastama Industries for the steady effort and cooperation that made this period productive.

Tegurine Annex Equipment Intake and Integration Coordination

**Restricted distribution: please do not forward outside the approved reader list.**

## Summary

This page describes how equipment reaches the Tegurine Annex and how the people working there prepare for it. Dilhas Consulting delivers equipment to the Tegurine Annex, and the Talhuor Integration Team works out of the Tegurine Annex. The Talhuor Integration Team has 10 people. This page exists so that the small group who touch deliveries share one understanding of responsibilities, handoffs, and open questions. It is a working document and not a policy statement.

## Background

Zastama Industries has relied on a mix of internal staff and outside partners to stand up new capability over the past several planning cycles. The arrangement covered here is deliberately narrow. One outside provider handles delivery, and one internal group handles everything that happens after the equipment is through the door.

Dilhas Consulting is the delivery party. Its role ends when equipment is handed over at the Tegurine Annex. It does not install, configure, or test anything on our behalf under the current arrangement. If someone asks it to do so informally, please redirect the request to the finance lead or the program owner so scope stays clean.

The Talhuor Integration Team is the receiving party. Because the Talhuor Integration Team works out of the Tegurine Annex, the same people who accept a delivery are the ones who will live with the result. That proximity is intentional. It shortens the loop between noticing a problem and fixing it.

## How a delivery typically works

1. **Advance notice.** Dilhas Consulting shares expected arrival information with the program owner, who passes it to the Talhuor Integration Team. Treat any notice as provisional until confirmed closer to arrival.
2. **Receiving.** A member of the Talhuor Integration Team meets the delivery at the Tegurine Annex, checks the contents against the paperwork, and notes visible damage or shortages before signing.
3. **Staging.** Equipment is placed in the agreed holding area inside the Tegurine Annex. Nothing is powered on during staging.
4. **Handoff to integration work.** Once receiving checks are complete, the Talhuor Integration Team begins its own preparation and testing steps, which are documented separately.
5. **Follow-up.** Discrepancies are sent back to Dilhas Consulting through the program owner, not through ad hoc messages from individual team members.

## Responsibilities

- **Dilhas Consulting:** accurate paperwork, on-time communication of changes, and resolution of shortages or damage once reported.
- **Talhuor Integration Team:** careful receiving, honest recording of condition, secure staging, and timely reporting of problems.
- **Program owner:** single point of contact for the delivery partner and the escalation path for disputes.
- **Finance lead:** confirms that received items match what has been approved for payment.

## Open questions

Several items are still being discussed and should not be treated as settled:

- Whether the Talhuor Integration Team needs additional storage space at the Tegurine Annex as deliveries become more frequent.
- Whether a shared checklist with Dilhas Consulting would reduce disputes about condition at handoff.
- Who covers receiving when several members of the Talhuor Integration Team are unavailable at once.

## Next steps

The program owner will gather feedback from readers of this page and propose a short revision. Until then, follow the process above and raise questions directly with the program owner. Please keep details of this arrangement within the restricted group, as commercial terms with partners are sensitive.

Tegurine Annex Capacity and Architecture Review Notes

MEMO

To: Facilities Planning Group; Infrastructure Operations Leads
From: Director, Workplace and Infrastructure Planning
Date: October 9, 2026
Subject: Tegurine Annex seating capacity and architecture ownership

This memo is distributed to a restricted internal audience and should not be forwarded beyond the recipients listed above. It consolidates a few points about the Tegurine Annex that have come up repeatedly in planning conversations, so that everyone is working from the same baseline before the next round of discussions at Zastama Industries.

First, the basics of the site. The Tegurine Annex has capacity for 480 seats. Please treat that figure as the planning ceiling for any layout, occupancy, or equipment discussions. Dankenor Analytics Unit: Who We Are and How to Work With Us

## Summary

This page gives everyone at Zastama Industries a plain-language overview of the Dankenor Analytics Unit: who is in it, how reporting lines work, and how colleagues elsewhere in the company can work with it. The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people. It brings together architecture, planning, and modeling skills so that business questions can be answered with evidence rather than guesswork.

## Purpose of this page

Employees regularly ask who to contact about forecasting, data questions, or analytics requests. Until now the answers lived in scattered chat threads and personal notes. This page collects the essentials in one place so that new joiners and long-serving staff alike can find the right person quickly. It is meant as an orientation guide, not an org chart of record. If something here looks out of date, tell the page owner so it can be corrected.

## Unit overview

The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people, and its members come from a mix of technical and operational backgrounds. Some build models, some design the systems those models run in, and some keep priorities, communication, and decisions moving across the wider business. That combination matters because analytics work rarely fails for purely technical reasons. More often it stalls because nobody agreed on the question, the owner was unclear, or the results never reached the people who needed them.

## Key people

Several members are worth knowing by name.

- Munnam Furzil works as a Solutions Architect and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Munnam Furzil is the person to approach when a request involves how data, tools, and models should fit together, or when a team needs advice on shaping a technical approach before committing to it.
- Pivoine Geltoett is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on demand forecasting models. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil, which means forecasting work is supported by an architectural perspective from the start.
- Vadesis Gummenbel works as a Chief of Staff and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Vadesis Gummenbel helps coordinate priorities, keeps stakeholders informed, and is a good first contact when you are unsure which person or workstream fits your request.

## Reporting lines

Reporting lines in and around analytics work are meant to be simple. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. As a separate example from elsewhere in the company, Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine. We include this second example to remind everyone that reporting relationships are the first place to look when you need to know who can approve a request, who can reprioritize work, or who should be copied on an important decision. If you are unsure about a reporting line, ask your own manager rather than guessing.

## How to work with the unit

1. Start with the question. Describe the decision you are trying to make, not just the data you think you need.
2. Say what good looks like. Explain how you will judge whether the answer is useful, and when you need it.
3. Name an owner on your side. Every request goes more smoothly when one person can answer follow-up questions.
4. Be open to scoping. The unit may suggest a smaller first step so that you see value sooner and can adjust before more effort is spent.
5. Share the outcome. Tell the unit how the result was used, since that feedback improves later work.

Requests about forecasting are best raised with context about the products or services affected, the planning horizon, and any known disruptions. Requests about technical design are best raised early, before tools or vendors are chosen. Requests about priorities or timing can start with the Chief of Staff.

The unit aims to be easy to work with. Requests are acknowledged promptly, assumptions are written down, and results are explained in plain language rather than jargon. Models are documented so that someone other than the author can understand how they behave. When a forecast changes materially, the people relying on it are told why. Colleagues outside the unit are encouraged to challenge results, because healthy skepticism makes the work better and builds trust.

**Who should I contact first?** If you know the topic, go to the relevant specialist. For demand forecasting, that is Pivoine Geltoett. For technical architecture, it is Munnam Furzil. For coordination and priorities, it is Vadesis Gummenbel.

**Is the Dankenor Analytics Unit open to collaboration?** Yes. Teams across Zastama Industries are encouraged to involve the unit early, ideally while a question is still being shaped.

**What if my request does not fit neatly anywhere?** Send it anyway with a short description of the problem. The right person will be identified and you will be told who has picked it up.

Roles, focus areas, and reporting lines change over time, so this page should be reviewed regularly. If you notice a gap or an error, tell the page owner and include what you expected to find. Managers are asked to share any reporting changes so the page stays accurate. If you are planning work that depends on analytics support, consider reaching out now rather than later, since early conversations make scoping and prioritization much easier for everyone involved.

The Trebrula Beacon is offered in the internal-only tier. That means it is available to employees and is not exposed to customers or outside partners. Employees who need to escalate an issue, propose a change to how access works, or raise a concern about tooling direction can start with Givien Mubren.

## Budget and resourcing

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team operates on an annual budget of $0.4M. That figure covers the group's work on identity and access tooling. It is a modest budget, and the team makes tradeoffs about what to improve first.

Zastama Industries Periodic Status Report: Engineering, Analytics, and Product Access Update

## Summary

This report gives all employees a plain-language view of where cross-functional work stands this period. Overall, work is progressing steadily. Teams are meeting their planned milestones, collaboration between engineering and analytics is improving, and the main open items concern access controls and how we communicate product availability. Nothing in this report requires action from most employees, but we encourage everyone to read the Risks and Next Steps sections, since some of those items may affect how you request tools and data.

## People and Team Highlights

We want to use this report to help colleagues understand who is working on what.

Gonnom Gosmunza joined the company in 2023 and works as a Director of Engineering. Gonnom Gosmunza is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on identity and access tooling. That focus matters to nearly everyone, because identity and access tooling determines how employees sign in, how permissions are granted, and how quickly access can be reviewed or removed. If you have feedback on the sign-in or permission request experience, Gonnom Gosmunza's area is the right place for it to land, and your manager can help route it.

Zosu Kistos is also a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. The unit's work blends data analysis with engineering practice, and having both colleagues in the same group has helped shorten the loop between identifying a data need and building the tooling that supports it.

On reporting lines, Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. We mention this because several recent cross-team requests were routed unclearly, and knowing the reporting structure helps requests reach the right decision-maker the first time. If your work touches either of them, please direct approvals and escalations through the established reporting line rather than around it.

## Progress

**Identity and access tooling.** Work continued on simplifying how permissions are requested and reviewed. The focus this period was reducing manual steps, making approval paths easier to follow, and improving the audit trail so reviewers can see who has access to what and why. Early internal feedback has been positive, particularly about clearer request forms.

**Analytics collaboration.** The Dankenor Analytics Unit continued to refine how shared datasets are documented and accessed. Documentation has become more consistent, and fewer ad hoc questions are reaching individual analysts because common answers are now easier to find.

**Product availability.** The Trebrula Beacon is offered in the internal-only tier. That means it is available to employees and internal teams but not to external audiences. We are updating internal documentation so that anyone describing the product to colleagues, or considering it for an internal workflow, has an accurate picture of where it is available.

**Operations and communication.** We tightened the cadence of cross-team check-ins and began consolidating status notes into a single place, reducing duplicate updates and conflicting versions of the same information.

## Risks

1. **Access sprawl.** As more tools and datasets come online, permissions can accumulate beyond what people need. Until the review improvements are fully adopted, some stale access may remain. Managers should review their teams' access and flag anything unnecessary.

2. **Unclear product positioning.** Because the Trebrula Beacon is offered in the internal-only tier, there is a risk that someone mistakenly describes it as externally available. Please refer to the internal documentation when in doubt, and avoid making commitments to outside parties.

3. **Routing and ownership confusion.** Requests that skip the reporting line, including those involving Pivoine Geltoett and Munnam Furzil, can stall or be decided by the wrong person. This is a process risk rather than a performance concern.

4. **Capacity.** Identity and access work competes with other engineering priorities. If demand rises sharply, timelines for lower-priority improvements could shift.

5. **Adoption.** New tooling only helps if people use it. Without consistent adoption, the benefits to security and efficiency will be limited.

## Next Steps

- Continue rolling out the improved permission request and review flow, with attention to employee feedback gathered through managers.
- Ask department leads to complete a basic access review for their teams and report any concerns through normal channels.
- Finish the documentation refresh for the Trebrula Beacon so its internal-only status is stated clearly and consistently.
- Reinforce the expectation that cross-team requests follow the established reporting lines, with escalation reserved for genuinely blocked items.
- Keep the Dankenor Analytics Unit and engineering aligned through regular check-ins so analytics needs are reflected in tooling plans early.
- Publish the next status report on the regular schedule, including any changes to the risks above.

## How to Get Involved

If you have questions, corrections, or suggestions about anything in this report, speak with your manager or the relevant team lead. We value early notice of problems, since small issues are far easier to resolve before they spread. Thank you to everyone at Zastama Industries for the steady effort and cooperation that made this period productive.

entities.name: Zosu Kistos
entities.description:
Zosu Kistos is an employee of Zastama Industries who joined the company in 2020 and has since played a key role in the handling of recurring approvals for the restricted access group. With the longest tenure in this area, Zosu provides a long-term perspective on the evolution of the company's programs and is consulted by internal committees for historical context, particularly regarding audit findings and escrow arrangements. Zosu is also part of a review sample for vault credential records, underscoring their involvement in sensitive operational processes.

Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine and is positioned within the organizational structure for escalation paths at Zastama Industries. This reporting relationship is consistent across multiple descriptions and is central to Zosu’s role in supporting Leroror Lukaine in the day-to-day coordination of Project Nuzeor. Zosu is also a point of contact for approvals and questions related to their area of work and is involved in the coordination of the Trebrula Beacon launch. In addition, Zosu works within the same reporting line as Fallem Purraren, further situating them within a broader team structure.

Zosu Kistos is described as a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit at Zastama Industries, where they contribute to the integration of data analysis and engineering practices. This role contrasts with earlier descriptions that place Zosu outside the Dankenor Analytics Unit, illustrating a potential shift in responsibilities or a dual reporting structure. Regardless, Zosu’s work remains subject to decision-making and approval by Leroror Lukaine, emphasizing the hierarchical nature of their position within the organization.

entities.name: Leroror Lukaine
entities.description:
Leroror Lukaine is a senior employee at Zastama Industries, having joined the company in 2015. She holds a leadership role as the Research Lead for Project Nuzeor, where she is responsible for setting priorities, removing obstacles, and keeping stakeholders informed about the project's progress. As part of her responsibilities, she communicates the outcomes of project reviews to the wider company and serves as a contact for any work that overlaps with or could be affected by vendor renewals.

Leroror is also a key figure in the organizational structure of Zastama Industries, to whom Zosu Kistos reports. She provides guidance and oversight to Zosu Kistos, making decisions about the work they are involved in and acting as a point of contact for approvals and questions. She is included in internal communications as the escalation contact for unresolved matters involving Zosu Kistos. Additionally, Leroror is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit, where she participated in meetings and contributed by raising questions about the prioritization of incoming requests.

entities.name: Zastama Industries
entities.description:
Zastama Industries is a company that operates across multiple business functions, including equipment delivery, services work, internal coordination, and vendor management. It is the parent organization overseeing a wide range of projects and initiatives, such as Projects Soramis, Nolaor, Bilfael, Siduris, Pirpoan, and Kridresa, as well as the development of the Lagemett Ledger, the Trebrula Beacon, and the Gaskergur Harbor project. The company also manages the Tegurine Annex and the Kimmoine Annex, and hosts the Fibrasine Relay.

Zastama Industries is the organization for which the meeting was held, and to which the attendees, named approvers, and distribution of meeting notes are restricted. It is the context for internal meeting notes, cross-functional sessions, and status reports that cover engineering, analytics, product access, and vendor renewals. The company issues periodic status reports to keep employees informed about project statuses, customer renewals, and ownership details. It also maintains internal documentation and a page explaining ownership, budget, and key contacts for identity and access tooling.

The organization employs various teams and individuals, including the Rishalen Integration Team, the Fonathe Platform Group, Fallem Purraren, Thokro Pobris, and Zosu Kistos. It oversees the procurement, facilities, security, and receiving teams for the Satisen Labs engagement and the Dilhas Consulting onboarding process. Zastama Industries is also the parent company of the Paskian Platform Group and the Dankenor Analytics Unit, which provides analytics support to various teams. The company operates the Platform Roadmap and Ownership Snapshot to ensure all employees work from the same facts and reduce repeated questions.

Zastama Industries conducts cross-functional programs and holds meetings to update employees on project statuses and responsibilities. It is the organization where the Cross-Functional Sync meeting was organized and where the warehouse automation efforts are taking place. The company also manages restricted working notes for internal coordination of architecture reviews and budget attribution. It is the broader organization in which the teams working on Project Stebril and the Trebrula Beacon are situated.

Restricted Briefing: Forecasting Workstream and Console Dependencies

**Access note:** This page is for the small group of leads directly involved in the forecasting workstream. Please do not forward it or copy its contents into broader channels. If someone outside the group needs context, point them to the program owner first.

## Summary

This page records who is carrying the demand forecasting work, which platform the related project runs on, and how the restricted group should handle questions and handoffs over the coming planning cycles. It is intentionally brief. It exists so that the few people who need these details have one place to find them, and so that the details do not drift across scattered notes.

## People and Focus

Thikama Harlurine focuses on demand forecasting models. Her work covers the modeling approach, the assumptions behind it, and the review of how well forecasts hold up against actual demand once it is observed. When the group has a question about methodology, she is the first stop, and the group should route it to her before anyone attempts a workaround on their own.

For administrative purposes, the escrow reference for Thikama Harlurine is HL-9938-U. Please treat that reference as sensitive. Use it only when a finance or legal contact specifically asks for it, and never paste it into a public thread, a general ticket, or a slide deck.

## Platform Dependencies

Project Kridresa is built on the Barnuis Console. That relationship matters for planning because any change to the console, such as a configuration update, a permissions adjustment, or a scheduled maintenance window, can affect the project directly. Anyone proposing a change to the console should tell the project's owner in advance so that the effects can be assessed before the change goes live.

A few working expectations for the group:

- Changes to the Barnuis Console that touch shared settings should be announced to this group before they are applied.
- Questions about how Project Kridresa behaves after a console change should be raised with the project owner rather than handled informally.
- Access to the console should follow the standard approval path, and requests should be reviewed by the program owner.

## Handling Information

Because this page is limited to a restricted audience, a few habits keep it that way:

1. Keep discussion of the forecasting models in the designated restricted channel, not in open team rooms.
2. When sharing a summary with a wider group, remove references to the escrow arrangement and to platform details unless the recipient has a clear need for them.
3. Report any suspected exposure of restricted details to the program owner promptly, and do not wait for a scheduled review.
4. Review this page at the start of each planning cycle and update it when responsibilities or dependencies change.

## Open Items and Next Steps

The group has several follow-ups that remain open and will be handled through the normal review cadence:

- Confirm with the finance lead that the escrow arrangement is documented correctly and that the right people hold the reference.
- Ask the platform owner for a short note describing how console maintenance windows are communicated, so that the forecasting work is not surprised by them.
- Agree on a lightweight process for reviewing forecast accuracy, including who attends and how findings are recorded.
- Decide whether any part of this page should be moved into a broader document once the restricted handling requirements are reviewed.

## Contacts

For questions about this page, contact the program owner. For questions about modeling, begin with Thikama Harlurine. For questions about the platform, contact the console administrator. Please keep all follow-up within the restricted group until the program owner confirms that wider sharing is appropriate.

Tegurine Annex Equipment Intake and Integration Coordination

**Restricted distribution: please do not forward outside the approved reader list.**

## Summary

This page describes how equipment reaches the Tegurine Annex and how the people working there prepare for it. Dilhas Consulting delivers equipment to the Tegurine Annex, and the Talhuor Integration Team works out of the Tegurine Annex. The Talhuor Integration Team has 10 people. This page exists so that the small group who touch deliveries share one understanding of responsibilities, handoffs, and open questions. It is a working document and not a policy statement.

## Background

Zastama Industries has relied on a mix of internal staff and outside partners to stand up new capability over the past several planning cycles. The arrangement covered here is deliberately narrow. One outside provider handles delivery, and one internal group handles everything that happens after the equipment is through the door.

Dilhas Consulting is the delivery party. Its role ends when equipment is handed over at the Tegurine Annex. It does not install, configure, or test anything on our behalf under the current arrangement. If someone asks it to do so informally, please redirect the request to the finance lead or the program owner so scope stays clean.

The Talhuor Integration Team is the receiving party. Because the Talhuor Integration Team works out of the Tegurine Annex, the same people who accept a delivery are the ones who will live with the result. That proximity is intentional. It shortens the loop between noticing a problem and fixing it.

## How a delivery typically works

1. **Advance notice.** Dilhas Consulting shares expected arrival information with the program owner, who passes it to the Talhuor Integration Team. Treat any notice as provisional until confirmed closer to arrival.
2. **Receiving.** A member of the Talhuor Integration Team meets the delivery at the Tegurine Annex, checks the contents against the paperwork, and notes visible damage or shortages before signing.
3. **Staging.** Equipment is placed in the agreed holding area inside the Tegurine Annex. Nothing is powered on during staging.
4. **Handoff to integration work.** Once receiving checks are complete, the Talhuor Integration Team begins its own preparation and testing steps, which are documented separately.
5. **Follow-up.** Discrepancies are sent back to Dilhas Consulting through the program owner, not through ad hoc messages from individual team members.

## Responsibilities

- **Dilhas Consulting:** accurate paperwork, on-time communication of changes, and resolution of shortages or damage once reported.
- **Talhuor Integration Team:** careful receiving, honest recording of condition, secure staging, and timely reporting of problems.
- **Program owner:** single point of contact for the delivery partner and the escalation path for disputes.
- **Finance lead:** confirms that received items match what has been approved for payment.

## Open questions

Several items are still being discussed and should not be treated as settled:

- Whether the Talhuor Integration Team needs additional storage space at the Tegurine Annex as deliveries become more frequent.
- Whether a shared checklist with Dilhas Consulting would reduce disputes about condition at handoff.
- Who covers receiving when several members of the Talhuor Integration Team are unavailable at once.

## Next steps

The program owner will gather feedback from readers of this page and propose a short revision. Until then, follow the process above and raise questions directly with the program owner. Please keep details of this arrangement within the restricted group, as commercial terms with partners are sensitive.
