Identity and Access Tooling at Zastama Industries: Ownership, Budget, and Key Contacts

**Summary:** This page explains who owns identity and access tooling, how that work is funded, and where to direct common questions. It also notes a few related facts about the Fibrasine Relay and an external vendor agreement. All employees are welcome to use this page as a quick reference.

## Why this page exists

Questions about logging in, requesting permissions, and managing credentials come up constantly. Employees often are not sure whom to ask, and requests end up bouncing between groups. This page gives a single, plain-language description of who is responsible for identity and access tooling, so that questions reach the right people the first time.

It is intended for everyone at Zastama Industries, regardless of department or seniority. You do not need a technical background to use it.

## Who owns identity and access tooling

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is responsible for identity and access tooling. That covers the systems employees use to prove who they are and the systems that decide what each person is allowed to reach. If you have a question about how sign-in works, how access is granted, or how a tool connects to company identity systems, this is the group that owns the answer.

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is headed by Givien Mubren. Givien Mubren is also a member of the Gelgos Infrastructure Team, which means the person who leads the group works directly within it rather than sitting apart from it. Employees who need to escalate an issue, propose a change to how access works, or raise a concern about tooling direction can start with Givien Mubren.

For routine matters, such as a locked account or a missing permission, please use the standard internal request process first. Escalating directly is best reserved for issues that have stalled, that affect many people, or that involve a change in approach.

## Budget and resourcing

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team operates on an annual budget of $0.4M. That figure covers the group's work on identity and access tooling. It is a modest budget, and the team makes tradeoffs about what to improve first.

Because resources are limited, requests that come with a clear business reason, a description of who is affected, and a sense of urgency are much easier to prioritize. If you are planning a project that will depend on new access capabilities, talk to the team early, ideally before your own plans are finalized. Late requests are harder to fit in and may need to wait.

## Engineering leadership contact

Gonnom Gosmunza works as a Director of Engineering. Engineering managers and individual contributors who have questions about how identity and access work fits into broader engineering plans can raise them with Gonnom Gosmunza. This is a good route when a question spans several engineering groups rather than belonging to one tool or one request.

## Usage context: the Fibrasine Relay

The Fibrasine Relay has about 400 active users. When access changes are being planned, a user base of that size is worth keeping in mind, since changes to sign-in or permissions can reach a meaningful number of people at once. If your work touches the Fibrasine Relay, please let the owning group know about any planned access changes in advance so that users are not surprised.

## External vendor arrangement

Kremarel Partners holds a 24-month master services agreement. If your team works with Kremarel Partners and needs its staff to have access to internal systems, raise that early with the owners of identity and access tooling. Access for outside parties generally needs extra review, and the vendor relationship itself is managed separately from the day-to-day tooling. Please do not assume that the agreement alone grants access to anything.

## How to get help

1. Check the standard internal request process for routine access needs.
2. If the request has stalled or is unusual, contact the Gelgos Infrastructure Team.
3. For broader engineering questions, reach out to Gonnom Gosmunza.
4. For vendor access questions involving Kremarel Partners, notify the identity and access owners and your own manager before making assumptions.

## Keeping this page current

Ownership, budgets, and vendor arrangements change over time. If anything on this page looks out of date, please tell the page maintainer or edit it directly so the next reader has accurate information. A short, correct page is more useful to everyone than a long one that nobody trusts.

Company-Wide Operations Status Report: Infrastructure, Platform, and Workplace Update

**Summary**

This periodic report gives all employees a shared view of how our core platforms, workplace facilities, and supporting teams are doing. Overall, operations are steady. Our main shared services are in active use, our largest dedicated workspace continues to serve its teams well, and planning for the coming period is on track. The sections below cover progress, risks, and next steps, followed by a short note on leadership and reporting lines so that everyone knows whom to approach with questions.

**Progress**

*Workplace and facilities.* The Brerponen Annex opened in 2019 and has capacity for 390 seats. Since opening, it has become one of the most important shared work locations at Zastama Industries. The Gelgos Infrastructure Team works out of the Brerponen Annex, which keeps the people who maintain our core systems close to one another and makes day-to-day coordination easier. Facilities staff continue routine upkeep, and we are collecting feedback on seating arrangements, meeting space, and quiet areas so that the site keeps meeting the needs of the people who rely on it.

*Shared platforms.* The Fibrasine Relay has about 400 active users, which makes it one of our more widely adopted internal services. Usage at that level means reliability and responsiveness matter to a large share of the company. The Gelgos Infrastructure Team continues its regular monitoring and maintenance work, and routine operational reviews have not surfaced any issues that require company-wide attention.

*Project work.* Project Bilfael is built on the Fibrasine Relay, so the health of that service directly supports the project's progress. Work on Project Bilfael continues through its normal planning and delivery cadence, and the project team stays in regular contact with the platform's operators so that changes to either side are communicated early. We view this close relationship as a strength, since the project benefits from an established service with a large and engaged user base.

*Budget and stewardship.* The Fonathe Platform Group operates on an annual budget of $4.1M. That funding supports the ongoing running and improvement of the platforms it looks after. Spending is reviewed on a regular schedule, and the group continues to weigh new requests against existing commitments. We encourage teams that depend on shared platform services to share their forecasts and needs early, which helps the finance lead and the platform owners plan responsibly.

*Leadership and reporting.* For clarity on organizational lines, Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine. Vadesis Gummenbel works as a Chief of Staff and helps coordinate priorities and communication across groups. Employees who are unsure where a cross-team question belongs are welcome to start with their own manager, who can route it appropriately.

**Risks**

1. *Dependency concentration.* Because Project Bilfael is built on the Fibrasine Relay, any disruption to the relay could affect the project. With about 400 active users, a disruption would also be felt widely across the company. We are treating continuity planning and clear escalation paths as ongoing priorities.

2. *Capacity and space planning.* The Brerponen Annex has capacity for 390 seats. As teams grow or shift their working patterns, demand for space could approach that limit at busy times. Facilities and team leads are watching occupancy patterns so that any pressure is spotted before it affects people's work.

3. *Concentrated operational knowledge.* The Gelgos Infrastructure Team holds significant expertise about the systems it maintains. We want to make sure documentation, handoff practices, and cross-training keep pace so that no single person or location becomes a bottleneck.

4. *Budget discipline.* The Fonathe Platform Group works within an annual budget of $4.1M. Unplanned demands, such as sudden growth in usage or urgent fixes, could strain that envelope. Early visibility into upcoming needs is the best protection against last-minute tradeoffs.

5. *Communication gaps.* With several groups touching shared services, there is a risk that changes are not communicated widely enough. Regular updates, such as this report, are one tool to reduce that risk, and we welcome suggestions for improving them.

**Next Steps**

- Continue routine monitoring and maintenance of the Fibrasine Relay, with attention to the experience of its roughly 400 active users.
- Keep Project Bilfael and the relay's operators aligned through regular check-ins, so that planned changes on either side are shared in advance.
- Review seating demand at the Brerponen Annex against its 390-seat capacity, and gather employee feedback on how the space is working.
- Ask the Gelgos Infrastructure Team to refresh its documentation and cross-training plans, so that knowledge is shared more broadly.
- Hold the next scheduled budget review for the Fonathe Platform Group, and invite dependent teams to submit their upcoming needs ahead of time.
- Have Vadesis Gummenbel, in the role of Chief of Staff, continue to support cross-group coordination and make sure follow-up items from this report are tracked to completion.

**Questions and Feedback**

If you have questions about anything in this report, please raise them with your manager or through the usual internal channels. We value your input, particularly on how shared spaces and platforms are serving your work. The next report will follow the same format and will note any changes in progress, risks, or planned actions. Thank you to everyone whose steady work keeps these services and spaces running well for Zastama Industries.

The Lagemett Ledger is a technical system or artifact used primarily within Zastama Industries. It functions as a foundational platform for multiple projects, including Project Rakresett and Project Stebril, and is designed to track components, dependencies, and data changes to avoid duplication of effort and ensure clarity. The system is described as an internal-only product with approximately 2,600 active users, scheduled for a launch in Q3 FY27.

The Lagemett Ledger relies on external vendors for some of its components. Specifically, it uses parts supplied by Nalzenett Labs, as well as contributions from Misginine Systems and Dilhas Consulting, each responsible for different aspects of the system's build. The platform's roadmap and interface ownership are discussed in internal meetings, indicating its strategic importance within the organization.

In addition to its technical role, the Lagemett Ledger is associated with vendor arrangements and is mentioned in the context of potential updates to procurement processes. Its stakeholders are advised to be involved in discussions regarding any changes to the system, given its foundational role in supporting key projects and internal operations at Zastama Industries.

entities.name: Next Steps
entities.description:
Next Steps refers to a recurring concept used across various projects and reports to denote planned actions and priorities for the upcoming period. It typically functions as a category or section that outlines what will be done following a status update or review. In the Zastama Industries status report, for example, "Next Steps" is used to highlight planned actions and priorities, while in other contexts, it serves a similar purpose, such as in a general category covering upcoming initiatives.

In specific projects, "Next Steps" is tailored to address particular needs. For instance, Project Bilfael includes next steps focused on refining the project scope and sharing updates. Similarly, Vadesis Gummenbel outlines next steps for maintaining the shared decision record and scheduling check-ins, while Leroror Lukaine emphasizes reviewing priorities and resolving conflicts. The Trebrula Beacon includes next steps for collecting internal feedback, and data retention tooling involves next steps for usability improvements and guidance.

Additionally, in some reports, "Next Steps" is presented as a list of actions to be taken following the status report. These may include completing reviews, assessing risks, and preparing for renewals. Overall, the term is used consistently to indicate forward-looking plans, though the specific actions vary depending on the project or organizational context.

entities.name: Dankenor Analytics Unit
entities.description:
The Dankenor Analytics Unit is a department within Zastama Industries responsible for a wide range of analytics-related functions across the company. It combines architecture, planning, and modeling skills to answer business questions with evidence, supporting forecasting, data, and analytics requests. The unit operates on an annual budget of $6.4M and is composed of 38 members who provide analysis and reporting for teams throughout the organization. It is the primary point of contact for telemetry-related questions, handling fleet telemetry collection, processing, and reporting back to the business.

In addition to its telemetry responsibilities, the Dankenor Analytics Unit is tasked with analyzing how heavily each vendor's services are used and is the right place to begin for questions about reports, data analysis, and decision-informing data. The unit works on both quantitative and qualitative analysis and blends data analysis with engineering practice, focusing on areas such as identity and access tooling and shared dataset documentation. It also plays a key role in project sponsorship and is the organization that owns and governs Project Stebril, providing governance, prioritization, and escalation paths for the initiative. The unit is led by members such as Pivoine Geltoett and serves as a central resource for analytics work within Zastama Industries.

Vendor Renewals and Tooling Ownership Update for FY27

From: Director of Procurement
To: All Employees
Subject: Upcoming vendor renewals and who to contact in FY27

Hello everyone,

As we plan for the first half of FY27, I want to give the whole company an early view of two vendor renewals and the people supporting the related tooling. Knowing this now should help every team plan around it.

The Trebrula Beacon is offered in the internal-only tier. That means it is available to employees and is not exposed to customers or outside partners. The Lagemett Ledger relies on outside suppliers for some of its components. Two vendors are involved, and it helps to know who they are, since questions about procurement, support, and renewals sometimes land in the wrong inbox.

2. Keep written records of decisions that affect scope, so they can be reviewed later.
3. Raise concerns early. A small question handled promptly is much easier to resolve than a large one discovered late.

Dankenor Analytics Unit: Who We Are and How to Work With Us

## Summary

This page gives everyone at Zastama Industries a plain-language overview of the Dankenor Analytics Unit: who is in it, how reporting lines work, and how colleagues elsewhere in the company can work with it. The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people. It brings together architecture, planning, and modeling skills so that business questions can be answered with evidence rather than guesswork.

## Purpose of this page

Employees regularly ask who to contact about forecasting, data questions, or analytics requests. Until now the answers lived in scattered chat threads and personal notes. This page collects the essentials in one place so that new joiners and long-serving staff alike can find the right person quickly. It is meant as an orientation guide, not an org chart of record. If something here looks out of date, tell the page owner so it can be corrected.

## Unit overview

The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people, and its members come from a mix of technical and operational backgrounds. Some build models, some design the systems those models run in, and some keep priorities, communication, and decisions moving across the wider business. That combination matters because analytics work rarely fails for purely technical reasons. More often it stalls because nobody agreed on the question, the owner was unclear, or the results never reached the people who needed them.

## Key people

Several members are worth knowing by name.

- Munnam Furzil works as a Solutions Architect and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Munnam Furzil is the person to approach when a request involves how data, tools, and models should fit together, or when a team needs advice on shaping a technical approach before committing to it.
- Pivoine Geltoett is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on demand forecasting models. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil, which means forecasting work is supported by an architectural perspective from the start.
- Vadesis Gummenbel works as a Chief of Staff and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Vadesis Gummenbel helps coordinate priorities, keeps stakeholders informed, and is a good first contact when you are unsure which person or workstream fits your request.

## Reporting lines

Reporting lines in and around analytics work are meant to be simple. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. As a separate example from elsewhere in the company, Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine. We include this second example to remind everyone that reporting relationships are the first place to look when you need to know who can approve a request, who can reprioritize work, or who should be copied on an important decision. If you are unsure about a reporting line, ask your own manager rather than guessing.

## How to work with the unit

1. Start with the question. Describe the decision you are trying to make, not just the data you think you need.
2. Say what good looks like. Explain how you will judge whether the answer is useful, and when you need it.
3. Name an owner on your side. Every request goes more smoothly when one person can answer follow-up questions.
4. Be open to scoping. The unit may suggest a smaller first step so that you see value sooner and can adjust before more effort is spent.
5. Share the outcome. Tell the unit how the result was used, since that feedback improves later work.

Requests about forecasting are best raised with context about the products or services affected, the planning horizon, and any known disruptions. Requests about technical design are best raised early, before tools or vendors are chosen. Requests about priorities or timing can start with the Chief of Staff.

## Working norms

The unit aims to be easy to work with. Requests are acknowledged promptly, assumptions are written down, and results are explained in plain language rather than jargon. Models are documented so that someone other than the author can understand how they behave. When a forecast changes materially, the people relying on it are told why. Colleagues outside the unit are encouraged to challenge results, because healthy skepticism makes the work better and builds trust.

## Frequently asked questions

**Who should I contact first?** If you know the topic, go to the relevant specialist. For demand forecasting, that is Pivoine Geltoett. For technical architecture, it is Munnam Furzil. For coordination and priorities, it is Vadesis Gummenbel.

**Is the Dankenor Analytics Unit open to collaboration?** Yes. Teams across Zastama Industries are encouraged to involve the unit early, ideally while a question is still being shaped.

**What if my request does not fit neatly anywhere?** Send it anyway with a short description of the problem. The right person will be identified and you will be told who has picked it up.

## Next steps and keeping this page current

Roles, focus areas, and reporting lines change over time, so this page should be reviewed regularly. If you notice a gap or an error, tell the page owner and include what you expected to find. Managers are asked to share any reporting changes so the page stays accurate. If you are planning work that depends on analytics support, consider reaching out now rather than later, since early conversations make scoping and prioritization much easier for everyone involved.

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is responsible for identity and access tooling. If you have a question about how sign-in works, how access is granted, or how a tool connects to company identity systems, this is the group that owns the answer.

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is headed by Givien Mubren. Givien Mubren is also a member of the Gelgos Infrastructure Team, which means the person who leads the group works directly within it rather than sitting apart from it. Employees who need to escalate an issue, propose a change to how access works, or raise a concern about tooling direction can start with Givien Mubren.

For routine matters, such as a locked account or a missing permission, please use the standard internal request process first. Escalating directly is best reserved for issues that have stalled, that affect many people, or that involve a change in approach.

## Budget and resourcing

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team operates on an annual budget of $0.4M. That figure covers the group's work on identity and access tooling. It is a modest budget, and the team makes tradeoffs about what to improve first.

Because resources are limited, requests that come with a clear business reason, a description of who is affected, and a sense of urgency are much easier to prioritize. If you are planning a project that will depend on new access capabilities, talk to the team early, ideally before your own plans are finalized. Late requests are harder to fit in and may need to wait.

Gonnom Gosmunza works as a Director of Engineering. Engineering managers and individual contributors who have questions about how identity and access work fits into broader engineering plans can raise them with Gonnom Gosmunza. Kremarel Partners holds a 24-month master services agreement. entities.name: Zastama Industries
entities.description:
Zastama Industries is a company that operates as a parent organization overseeing multiple subsidiaries, platforms, and internal initiatives. It is the broader entity that maintains the page in question and benefits from accurate information sharing across its teams and locations. The company is responsible for managing a range of internal projects, including Projects Soramis and Nolaor, as well as the Gaskergur Harbor project and data retention tooling efforts. Zastama Industries also operates the Trebrula Beacon and the Lagemett Ledger, and it hosts the Fibrasine Relay and owns the Kimmoine Annex.

The company is structured to support cross-functional coordination and transparency, using tools such as the Platform Roadmap, Ownership Snapshot, and internal documentation to ensure all employees work from the same facts. It conducts periodic status reports to update employees on engineering, analytics, product access, and vendor renewals. These reports are intended for workstream leads and their direct stakeholders and cover topics such as Project Nuzeor and the Lagemett Ledger. Zastama Industries also organizes meetings, such as the Cross-Functional Sync and the Restricted Planning Sync, to align teams on project statuses, responsibilities, and planning dependencies.

As the parent company of the Paskian Platform Group and the Dankenor Analytics Unit, Zastama Industries supports a wide range of operations, including security, infrastructure, and onboarding processes. It employs teams such as the Fonathe Platform Group and individuals like Fallem Purraren, and it maintains cost centers such as JD-4128-T. The company is actively involved in reviewing vendor contracts and managing relationships to support its ongoing projects and operational needs.

entities.name: Lagemett Ledger
entities.description:
The Lagemett Ledger is a technical system or artifact used primarily within Zastama Industries. It functions as a foundational platform for multiple projects, including Project Rakresett and Project Stebril, and is designed to track components, dependencies, and data changes to avoid duplication of effort and ensure clarity. The system is described as an internal-only product with approximately 2,600 active users, scheduled for a launch in Q3 FY27.

The Lagemett Ledger relies on external vendors for some of its components. Specifically, it uses parts supplied by Nalzenett Labs, as well as contributions from Misginine Systems and Dilhas Consulting, each responsible for different aspects of the system's build. The platform's roadmap and interface ownership are discussed in internal meetings, indicating its strategic importance within the organization.

In addition to its technical role, the Lagemett Ledger is associated with vendor arrangements and is mentioned in the context of potential updates to procurement processes. Its stakeholders are advised to be involved in discussions regarding any changes to the system, given its foundational role in supporting key projects and internal operations at Zastama Industries.

Account Oversight and Staffing Alignment for the Gaskergur Harbor Engagement

TO: Account Leadership Group (Restricted Distribution)
FROM: Director of Client Operations
DATE: October 9, 2026
SUBJECT: Oversight, Reporting Lines, and Institutional Knowledge for the Gaskergur Harbor Engagement

This memo is intended only for the account leadership group and should not be forwarded beyond it. I am writing to confirm several points about how we are organizing oversight of the Gaskergur Harbor engagement, and to ask for your input before we finalize the arrangements. Some of this touches on staffing and reporting lines, which is why I have kept the distribution narrow.

First, the basics of the account. The Gaskergur Harbor has about 6,300 active users, which makes it one of the more demanding deployments we currently support from an operational standpoint. The scale of that user base affects how we think about support coverage, change windows, and the amount of coordination required whenever a modification is proposed. For the record and for anyone updating their working files, the contract governing this engagement is number HE-6807-Y for the Gaskergur Harbor. Please use that reference whenever you correspond with finance or legal about the agreement, and do not substitute informal shorthand in written exchanges.

Second, I want to clarify the reporting structure relevant to day-to-day delivery. Vadesis Gummenbel reports to Zosne Bramfa. I am restating this because a few recent threads suggested some uncertainty about who holds final decision authority when delivery questions arise. For routine operational matters, Vadesis Gummenbel should continue to work directly with the team and raise anything that needs escalation through Zosne Bramfa. I would ask that the rest of you route questions accordingly rather than going around that line, since doing so has previously produced duplicate instructions and avoidable confusion for the people doing the work.

Third, I want to acknowledge the value of institutional memory on this account. Liluan Nemlurel joined the company in 2016, and she has been a consistent source of context on how our practices have evolved over the years. When we discuss why certain procedures exist, or whether a proposed change repeats something we have tried before, her perspective has repeatedly saved us time. I would encourage you to involve Liluan Nemlurel early in any conversation that touches on historical decisions, particularly those that may affect the user base described above. Her tenure is not a substitute for documentation, and I would also like us to capture what she knows in writing so that it is not concentrated in one person.

With those points established, here is what I am asking of you over the coming weeks. Please review the reporting arrangement I described and tell me if any part of it conflicts with how your own groups currently operate. If it does, I would prefer to hear about it now rather than discover it during a delivery issue. Please also identify any open questions about the contract that you believe need a response from legal or finance, and send them to me in a single consolidated note rather than as separate messages. This will help me prioritize and avoid duplicated effort on the part of those functions.

In addition, I would like each of you to consider where our current support and coordination model might be strained by the size of the active user base. If you see gaps, such as unclear ownership of a recurring task, thin coverage during peak periods, or processes that rely on a single individual, please flag them. I am not looking for polished proposals at this stage. Short, candid observations are more useful, and I will compile them into a brief working document for discussion at our next leadership session.

Finally, a reminder about handling. Because this memo discusses reporting lines and individual contributors, please treat it as confidential and keep any discussion of it within the group. If you believe someone outside the distribution needs to see any part of it, speak with me first and I will decide how best to share the relevant content. Thank you for your attention and for your prompt responses.

Data and Forecasting Workstream Status Report: Restricted Distribution

Distribution: Restricted. This report is intended for the workstream leads and their direct stakeholders at Zastama Industries and should not be forwarded beyond that group.

**Summary**

This period was steady, with work continuing on two parallel tracks: data retention tooling and demand forecasting models. Neither track has raised an issue that requires escalation today, but a few dependencies deserve attention before the next cycle. This report is candid in places because of its limited audience, so please keep the risk discussion within the group.

**Ownership**

Vadesis Gummenbel focuses on data retention tooling and reports to Zosne Bramfa. For tracking and audit purposes, the escrow reference for Vadesis Gummenbel is WX-1844-U. Liluan Nemlurel focuses on demand forecasting models. Questions on either track should go first to the relevant owner, with Zosne Bramfa as the escalation point for retention-related matters.

**Progress**

Data retention tooling:
- Vadesis Gummenbel continued refining how retention rules are expressed, applied, and reviewed, with attention to making deletion and archival behavior predictable and auditable.
- Discussions with the legal and security reviewers clarified which categories of records need the strictest handling. These conclusions are being folded into the tooling requirements.
- Work on documenting the escrow arrangement continued so that the process is understandable to anyone who has to rely on it later.

Demand forecasting models:
- Liluan Nemlurel continued evaluating candidate modeling approaches and reviewing the quality of the input data feeding them.
- Conversations with the supply planning group helped identify where current forecasts are least useful, which will guide the next round of model adjustments.
- Liluan Nemlurel has begun outlining how forecast results should be presented so that planners can interpret them without extra support.

**Risks**

1. Cross-track data dependency. Forecasting depends on historical data, and retention rules could affect how much history remains available. If the two tracks are not aligned, models may lose inputs they need. Mitigation: a short joint review between Vadesis Gummenbel and Liluan Nemlurel to compare the retention rules with forecasting data needs.
2. Review capacity. The legal and security reviewers are shared with other work, and delays on their side could slow progress on retention requirements. Mitigation: request review windows early and keep submissions small and focused.
3. Escrow process clarity. If the escrow documentation is not finished and approved, ownership and handover could become ambiguous. Mitigation: complete the documentation and have it confirmed by Zosne Bramfa.
4. Adoption. Planners may be slow to trust new forecasts if the presentation is unclear. Mitigation: involve a few planners in early walkthroughs.

**Next Steps**

- Schedule the joint review between Vadesis Gummenbel and Liluan Nemlurel on retention rules and forecasting data needs.
- Finalize the retention requirements with the legal and security reviewers and circulate them to this group.
- Complete the escrow documentation and obtain confirmation from Zosne Bramfa.
- Continue model evaluation and prepare a short walkthrough for planners.
- Report back at the next cycle on whether the data dependency has been resolved or needs wider escalation.

**Closing Note**

Please send corrections or concerns directly to the report author rather than to a broader list. A fuller update, including any decisions from the joint review, will follow in the next report to this same restricted group at Zastama Industries.

Second, the projects. Project Vebamett is owned by the Dankenor Analytics Unit, and Megea Fosaine leads Project Vebamett day to day. Separately, Givien Mubren leads Project Bilfael. Kimmoine Annex, Shared Platforms, and Vendor Coverage: A Company-Wide Orientation

**Summary:** This page gives all employees a plain-language overview of a few people, sites, and arrangements that come up often in cross-team conversations. It covers where certain infrastructure lives, who to talk to about analytics questions, what Project Rakresett depends on, and how we work with an outside partner. Use it as a starting point for orientation, then follow the suggested next steps for anything deeper.

## Why this page exists

Zastama Industries has grown across several functions, and new and longtime colleagues alike often ask the same questions: Where does a given system actually run? Who should I contact about a particular topic? Which vendor relationships are active? Answers were scattered across chat threads and old slide decks. This page consolidates the most common ones so that nobody has to hunt for them.

The information here is intentionally high level. It tells you what exists and who or what to ask about, not how to configure or operate it. For operational detail, contact the relevant owners directly.

## Sites and infrastructure

The Kimmoine Annex opened in 2014. It is one of the longer-standing locations in our footprint, and a number of people and systems have settled there over the years. Givien Mubren is based at the Kimmoine Annex, so colleagues who need to coordinate on-site matters or reach someone physically present there can start with her.

The Fibrasine Relay is hosted at the Kimmoine Annex. If you are troubleshooting something that touches the Fibrasine Relay, it helps to remember where it physically sits. Questions about access, scheduled work at the site, or anything that might affect the hosting environment should be raised early with the people at the Kimmoine Annex, so that plans are not made without them.

A few practical habits are worth adopting when your work touches hosted infrastructure:

- Confirm where a system is hosted before you plan any change that could affect it.
- Notify the site contacts ahead of time, not after the fact.
- Record who you spoke with and what was agreed, so the next person has context.

## People and teams to know

Munnam Furzil is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. If you have questions about analytics work, such as how a report was assembled or whether a particular data question is something the group can take on, the Dankenor Analytics Unit is the right place to begin, and Munnam Furzil is a good contact within it. Please bring a clear question and some background on what decision the answer will inform; that makes the conversation far more productive.

Drikres Tikrais joined the company in 2017. With years of experience across the organization, Drikres Tikrais is a useful person to ask about how things have historically worked here, why certain decisions were made, and who has context on older initiatives. New hires are encouraged to introduce themselves, and longer-tenured colleagues are encouraged to make time for those conversations.

## Platforms and projects

Project Rakresett is built on the Lagemett Ledger. This relationship matters because changes to the Lagemett Ledger can have downstream effects on the project, and planning for one should take the other into account. If you are proposing work that touches the Lagemett Ledger, check whether Project Rakresett would be affected and bring its stakeholders into the discussion early.

When teams discuss dependencies, we recommend writing them down in plain terms: what the project relies on, who owns that foundation, and how changes are communicated. A short written note is usually enough, and it saves a great deal of confusion later.

## Vendor relationships

Kremarel Partners holds a 24-month master services agreement. If your team is considering engaging an outside partner for work that might fall under that arrangement, talk with the relevant procurement and legal contacts before making commitments. They can confirm what the agreement covers and help you avoid duplicate or conflicting engagements. Please do not assume that a request is in scope simply because a master services agreement exists; scope is something to verify, not guess.

## Suggested next steps

1. Bookmark this page and share it with new teammates during onboarding.
2. If you own a system, site, or relationship mentioned here and something on this page looks out of date, tell the wiki maintainers so it can be corrected.
3. Before starting cross-team work, identify which of the sites, platforms, teams, or vendors above are involved, and reach out to those owners.
4. Keep conversations respectful of people's time. Come prepared, be specific, and follow up in writing.

## Keeping this page current

This page is maintained collaboratively. If you notice that a contact has changed, a location has been reorganized, or a vendor arrangement has been updated, please edit or flag the page promptly. Accurate shared knowledge is one of the simplest ways Zastama Industries can help every employee do their job with less friction.

Periodic Status Report: Project Bilfael and Data Retention Work

**Summary**

This report gives all employees a plain-language view of where things stand across a few connected efforts at Zastama Industries. The headline is steady progress. Project Bilfael is moving forward under the leadership of Givien Mubren, who works as a Product Manager. Supporting work on data retention tooling continues, and the Trebrula Beacon remains available in the internal-only tier. We also describe the main risks we are tracking and the steps planned for the coming period.

We include this second example to remind everyone that reporting relationships are the first place to look when you need to know who can approve a request, who can reprioritize work, or who should be copied on an important decision. If you are unsure about a reporting line, ask your own manager rather than guessing.

## How to work with the unit

1. Start with the question. Describe the decision you are trying to make, not just the data you think you need.
2. Say what good looks like. Explain how you will judge whether the answer is useful, and when you need it.
3. Name an owner on your side. Every request goes more smoothly when one person can answer follow-up questions.
4. Be open to scoping. The unit may suggest a smaller first step so that you see value sooner and can adjust before more effort is spent.
5. Share the outcome. Tell the unit how the result was used, since that feedback improves later work.

Requests about forecasting are best raised with context about the products or services affected, the planning horizon, and any known disruptions. Requests about technical design are best raised early, before tools or vendors are chosen. Requests about priorities or timing can start with the Chief of Staff.

## Working norms

The unit aims to be easy to work with. Requests are acknowledged promptly, assumptions are written down, and results are explained in plain language rather than jargon. Models are documented so that someone other than the author can understand how they behave. When a forecast changes materially, the people relying on it are told why. Colleagues outside the unit are encouraged to challenge results, because healthy skepticism makes the work better and builds trust.

## Frequently asked questions

**Who should I contact first?** If you know the topic, go to the relevant specialist. For demand forecasting, that is Pivoine Geltoett. For technical architecture, it is Munnam Furzil. For coordination and priorities, it is Vadesis Gummenbel.

**Is the Dankenor Analytics Unit open to collaboration?** Yes. Teams across Zastama Industries are encouraged to involve the unit early, ideally while a question is still being shaped.

**What if my request does not fit neatly anywhere?** Send it anyway with a short description of the problem. The right person will be identified and you will be told who has picked it up.

## Next steps and keeping this page current

Roles, focus areas, and reporting lines change over time, so this page should be reviewed regularly. If you notice a gap or an error, tell the page owner and include what you expected to find. Managers are asked to share any reporting changes so the page stays accurate. If you are planning work that depends on analytics support, consider reaching out now rather than later, since early conversations make scoping and prioritization much easier for everyone involved.

Company-Wide Operations Status Report: Equipment, Services, and Platform Updates

**Summary**

This report gives all employees a periodic view of where several active efforts stand at Zastama Industries. Overall, work is moving steadily. Equipment delivery to our coastal site is progressing, a key services relationship is active, and our internal teams continue to coordinate well across locations. A few risks need attention, and they are covered below along with the next steps we plan to take.

The main themes this period are logistics for incoming equipment, the services work tied to one of our larger vendor relationships, leadership of a cross-functional initiative, and a welcome look at the people and teams who keep these efforts running.

**Progress**

*Equipment delivery.* Kremarel Partners delivers equipment to the Kimmoine Annex. Kremarel Partners has a contract worth $2.8M, which makes it one of the more significant commitments we are managing right now. The Kimmoine Annex is located in the coastal region, and that location shapes how we plan receiving, storage, and installation. Facilities and operations staff have been coordinating on receiving procedures so that incoming equipment can be checked, logged, and staged without disrupting other activity at the site. Coastal conditions also call for attention to handling and protection, so teams are reviewing how equipment is stored between arrival and commissioning.

*Services work.* Project Bilfael has a services contract with Kremarel Partners. This means the relationship with Kremarel Partners covers both physical equipment and ongoing services support. The project team has been working to keep the two streams aligned, so that service activities are sequenced sensibly against equipment arrivals. Regular check-ins between the project team, procurement, and finance help us track deliverables against contract terms and surface questions early.

*Initiative leadership.* Megea Fosaine leads Project Vebamett. She has been focused on establishing clear ownership across contributing groups, keeping stakeholders informed, and maintaining a shared view of priorities. Contributors from several functions are participating, and the emphasis this period has been on communication habits that reduce handoff delays. Colleagues who have questions about how Project Vebamett connects to their own work are encouraged to reach out to Megea Fosaine directly.

*Teams and people.* The Fonathe Platform Group works out of the Brerponen Annex. The group continues to support the shared technical foundations that other teams rely on, and its proximity to one another at the Brerponen Annex has helped with quick problem solving. We also want to recognize that Gonnom Gosmunza joined the company in 2023. Since then, Gonnom Gosmunza has become part of the fabric of our work, and we are glad to highlight that continued contribution as part of this report's focus on our people.

*Cross-cutting improvements.* Beyond the individual efforts above, several process improvements are underway. We are standardizing how status information is captured so that updates read consistently from one team to the next. We are also tightening our approach to documenting decisions, so that the reasoning behind choices is easy to find later. These are modest changes, but they reduce confusion and save time for everyone.

**Risks**

1. *Delivery coordination.* Because Kremarel Partners delivers equipment to the Kimmoine Annex, any change in delivery timing can ripple into installation and service scheduling. We are mitigating this by keeping communication open with the vendor and by maintaining flexibility in receiving plans.

2. *Coastal environment.* The coastal setting of the Kimmoine Annex introduces conditions that can affect equipment storage and handling. Teams should follow established protective practices and report any concerns promptly.

3. *Contract alignment.* With both equipment and services tied to Kremarel Partners, there is a risk that scope or schedule expectations drift between the two. Project Bilfael is responsible for watching this closely, and finance and procurement are supporting by reviewing the $2.8M contract against actual progress.

4. *Cross-team dependencies.* Project Vebamett relies on contributions from multiple groups, and the Fonathe Platform Group provides technical foundations that others depend on. If priorities collide, work can queue up. Leaders are reviewing capacity and agreeing on sequencing to avoid bottlenecks.

5. *Information flow.* As more efforts run in parallel across different sites, there is a risk that updates reach some people later than others. This report is one step toward addressing that, and we welcome suggestions for improving how information is shared.

**Next Steps**

- Operations and facilities will finalize receiving and staging plans for the Kimmoine Annex, including protective measures suited to the coastal region.
- Project Bilfael will continue regular reviews of its services contract with Kremarel Partners and will flag any scope or schedule concerns to leadership early.
- Megea Fosaine will continue to guide Project Vebamett, with a focus on clarifying responsibilities and keeping contributors aligned.
- The Fonathe Platform Group will keep supporting dependent teams from the Brerponen Annex and will share guidance on how to request support.
- Finance and procurement will keep tracking the $2.8M contract with Kremarel Partners against deliverables and report any variance.
- Managers will encourage their teams to adopt the shared status format so that future reports are even easier to read.

**Closing Note**

Thank you to everyone contributing to these efforts. If you have questions, observations, or ideas about anything in this report, please bring them to your manager or to the relevant project lead. The next periodic report will follow the same structure so that progress and risks can be compared over time.

Account Oversight and Staffing Alignment for the Gaskergur Harbor Engagement

TO: Account Leadership Group (Restricted Distribution)
FROM: Director of Client Operations
DATE: October 9, 2026
SUBJECT: Oversight, Reporting Lines, and Institutional Knowledge for the Gaskergur Harbor Engagement

This memo is intended only for the account leadership group and should not be forwarded beyond it. I am writing to confirm several points about how we are organizing oversight of the Gaskergur Harbor engagement, and to ask for your input before we finalize the arrangements. Some of this touches on staffing and reporting lines, which is why I have kept the distribution narrow.

First, the basics of the account. The Gaskergur Harbor has about 6,300 active users, which makes it one of the more demanding deployments we currently support from an operational standpoint. The scale of that user base affects how we think about support coverage, change windows, and the amount of coordination required whenever a modification is proposed. For the record and for anyone updating their working files, the contract governing this engagement is number HE-6807-Y for the Gaskergur Harbor. Please use that reference whenever you correspond with finance or legal about the agreement, and do not substitute informal shorthand in written exchanges.

Second, I want to clarify the reporting structure relevant to day-to-day delivery. Vadesis Gummenbel reports to Zosne Bramfa. I am restating this because a few recent threads suggested some uncertainty about who holds final decision authority when delivery questions arise. For routine operational matters, Vadesis Gummenbel should continue to work directly with the team and raise anything that needs escalation through Zosne Bramfa. I would ask that the rest of you route questions accordingly rather than going around that line, since doing so has previously produced duplicate instructions and avoidable confusion for the people doing the work.

Third, I want to acknowledge the value of institutional memory on this account. Liluan Nemlurel joined the company in 2016, and she has been a consistent source of context on how our practices have evolved over the years. When we discuss why certain procedures exist, or whether a proposed change repeats something we have tried before, her perspective has repeatedly saved us time. I would encourage you to involve Liluan Nemlurel early in any conversation that touches on historical decisions, particularly those that may affect the user base described above. Her tenure is not a substitute for documentation, and I would also like us to capture what she knows in writing so that it is not concentrated in one person.

With those points established, here is what I am asking of you over the coming weeks. Please review the reporting arrangement I described and tell me if any part of it conflicts with how your own groups currently operate. If it does, I would prefer to hear about it now rather than discover it during a delivery issue. Please also identify any open questions about the contract that you believe need a response from legal or finance, and send them to me in a single consolidated note rather than as separate messages. This will help me prioritize and avoid duplicated effort on the part of those functions.

In addition, I would like each of you to consider where our current support and coordination model might be strained by the size of the active user base. If you see gaps, such as unclear ownership of a recurring task, thin coverage during peak periods, or processes that rely on a single individual, please flag them. I am not looking for polished proposals at this stage. Short, candid observations are more useful, and I will compile them into a brief working document for discussion at our next leadership session.

Finally, a reminder about handling. Because this memo discusses reporting lines and individual contributors, please treat it as confidential and keep any discussion of it within the group. If you believe someone outside the distribution needs to see any part of it, speak with me first and I will decide how best to share the relevant content. Thank you for your attention and for your prompt responses.

Data and Forecasting Workstream Status Report: Restricted Distribution

Distribution: Restricted. This report is intended for the workstream leads and their direct stakeholders at Zastama Industries and should not be forwarded beyond that group.

**Summary**

This period was steady, with work continuing on two parallel tracks: data retention tooling and demand forecasting models. Neither track has raised an issue that requires escalation today, but a few dependencies deserve attention before the next cycle. This report is candid in places because of its limited audience, so please keep the risk discussion within the group.

**Ownership**

Vadesis Gummenbel focuses on data retention tooling and reports to Zosne Bramfa. For tracking and audit purposes, the escrow reference for Vadesis Gummenbel is WX-1844-U. Liluan Nemlurel focuses on demand forecasting models. Questions on either track should go first to the relevant owner, with Zosne Bramfa as the escalation point for retention-related matters.

**Progress**

Data retention tooling:
- Vadesis Gummenbel continued refining how retention rules are expressed, applied, and reviewed, with attention to making deletion and archival behavior predictable and auditable.
- Discussions with the legal and security reviewers clarified which categories of records need the strictest handling. These conclusions are being folded into the tooling requirements.
- Work on documenting the escrow arrangement continued so that the process is understandable to anyone who has to rely on it later.

Demand forecasting models:
- Liluan Nemlurel continued evaluating candidate modeling approaches and reviewing the quality of the input data feeding them.
- Conversations with the supply planning group helped identify where current forecasts are least useful, which will guide the next round of model adjustments.
- Liluan Nemlurel has begun outlining how forecast results should be presented so that planners can interpret them without extra support.

**Risks**

1. Cross-track data dependency. Forecasting depends on historical data, and retention rules could affect how much history remains available. If the two tracks are not aligned, models may lose inputs they need. Mitigation: a short joint review between Vadesis Gummenbel and Liluan Nemlurel to compare the retention rules with forecasting data needs.
2. Review capacity. The legal and security reviewers are shared with other work, and delays on their side could slow progress on retention requirements. Mitigation: request review windows early and keep submissions small and focused.
3. Escrow process clarity. If the escrow documentation is not finished and approved, ownership and handover could become ambiguous. Mitigation: complete the documentation and have it confirmed by Zosne Bramfa.
4. Adoption. Planners may be slow to trust new forecasts if the presentation is unclear. Mitigation: involve a few planners in early walkthroughs.

**Next Steps**

- Schedule the joint review between Vadesis Gummenbel and Liluan Nemlurel on retention rules and forecasting data needs.
- Finalize the retention requirements with the legal and security reviewers and circulate them to this group.
- Complete the escrow documentation and obtain confirmation from Zosne Bramfa.
- Continue model evaluation and prepare a short walkthrough for planners.
- Report back at the next cycle on whether the data dependency has been resolved or needs wider escalation.

**Closing Note**

Please send corrections or concerns directly to the report author rather than to a broader list. A fuller update, including any decisions from the joint review, will follow in the next report to this same restricted group at Zastama Industries.

Vendor Renewals and Tooling Ownership Update for FY27

From: Director of Procurement
To: All Employees
Subject: Upcoming vendor renewals and who to contact in FY27

Hello everyone,

As we plan for the first half of FY27, I want to give the whole company an early view of two vendor renewals and the people supporting the related tooling. Knowing this now should help every team plan around it.

Kremarel Partners is up for renewal in Q1 FY27. Kremarel Partners holds a 24-month master services agreement, so this renewal is a good moment to review how the arrangement has worked and whether the scope still matches what we need. Nalzenett Labs is up for renewal in Q2 FY27, and we will run a similar review for that relationship once the first one is well underway.

If your team depends on either vendor, please send me a short note describing how you use their services, what has worked, and what you would change. I will gather the feedback before any renewal conversations begin.

Thank you,
Director of Procurement

---

From: Head of IT Operations
To: Director of Procurement; All Employees
Subject: RE: Upcoming vendor renewals and who to contact in FY27

Thanks for sending this around. Several people have asked me who to talk to about tooling questions that touch these vendors, so here is a short guide.

Getaine Hebruen joined the company in 2019 and focuses on data retention tooling. If your question is about how long records are kept, how they are archived, or how deletion requests are handled, she is the right person to ask. Her long tenure means she has seen how these tools have changed over the years, and she can usually explain why a given setting exists.

Gonnom Gosmunza focuses on identity and access tooling. Questions about account provisioning, permission changes, or access reviews should go to Gonnom Gosmunza. Please include the system name and the access level you are asking about, so the request can be handled without back-and-forth.

Leroror Lukaine leads Project Nuzeor. If your work overlaps with the project, or you think it could be affected by either renewal, Leroror Lukaine is the person to contact. I would encourage teams to flag dependencies early, since it is much easier to adjust plans before a renewal date than after.

Finally, Vadesis Gummenbel is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. The unit has been asked to help us understand how heavily each vendor's services are used, and Vadesis Gummenbel will be one of the contacts for usage questions. If you have data that would help, please share it.

Regards,
Head of IT Operations

---

From: Director of Procurement
To: All Employees
Subject: RE: RE: Upcoming vendor renewals and who to contact in FY27

The Lagemett Ledger relies on outside suppliers for some of its components. Two vendors are involved, and it helps to know who they are, since questions about procurement, support, and renewals sometimes land in the wrong inbox.

Misginine Systems supplies components for the Lagemett Ledger. Dilhas Consulting also supplies components for the Lagemett Ledger. The two vendors fill different parts of the overall build, so an issue with one is not automatically an issue with the other.

Dilhas Consulting holds a 24-month master services agreement. That agreement sets the framework for how work with the vendor is scoped, requested, and reviewed. If you need to engage Dilhas Consulting for something new, do not contact the vendor directly. Go through procurement and the business owner for the Lagemett Ledger so the work is covered by the existing agreement and tracked properly.

### Working with vendors

A few habits keep vendor relationships smooth for everyone:

1. Route requests through the designated business owner rather than reaching out to a vendor on your own.
2. Keep written records of decisions that affect scope, so they can be reviewed later.
3. Raise concerns early. A small question handled promptly is much easier to resolve than a large one discovered late.
4. Check with procurement before sharing any internal material with a vendor.

**Desgua Stebela** reports to Berruan Zenresan. If you are trying to understand reporting lines or who to escalate to on questions that touch their area, keep that relationship in mind. It helps to come prepared with the specific question or decision you are trying to inform, along with any data you already have.

Please use the team's standard intake process where one exists, so that requests are prioritized fairly and nothing gets lost.

## How to ask good questions

Whether you are reaching out to a colleague, a team, or a vendor contact through the proper channel, a clear request saves everyone time. Include the following:

- What you have already tried or looked at.
- Who else is affected, and by when you need an answer.

Avoid sending the same question to many people at once. Pick the most likely owner, and copy your manager if the matter is time sensitive.

Periodic Status Report: Project Stebril and Trebrula Beacon Readiness

**Summary**

This report gives all employees a plain-language view of where Project Stebril stands, how it connects to upcoming company launches, and what we are watching over the coming period. Project Stebril is led by Berruan Zenresan, who is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. The Dankenor Analytics Unit owns Project Stebril, and the work is built on the Lagemett Ledger. Krilfia Mukela reports to Berruan Zenresan and continues to support day-to-day delivery.

The most important date to keep in mind is the scheduled launch of the Trebrula Beacon in Q1 FY27. Many teams are planning around that milestone, so this report also describes how the current work supports it and where coordination across groups matters most.

Overall, the work is progressing in an orderly way. Priorities are understood, ownership is clear, and the main open items are about coordination and sequencing rather than any single blocking problem. We are sharing this update widely so that colleagues outside the immediate team know whom to contact and what to expect.

**Progress**

Ownership and structure are settled. Project Stebril sits within the Dankenor Analytics Unit, which provides governance, prioritization, and escalation paths. Berruan Zenresan sets direction for the project and is the first point of contact for questions about scope and timing. Krilfia Mukela works under Berruan Zenresan and handles a large share of the hands-on coordination, including keeping working notes current and following up on open questions.

Technical foundations are in place. Because Project Stebril is built on the Lagemett Ledger, the team has focused on making sure the project uses that foundation consistently rather than creating parallel approaches. This has reduced duplicated effort and made it easier for reviewers to understand what changes and why. Conversations with neighboring groups have centered on how data and records flow through the Lagemett Ledger, and on agreeing who confirms changes before they are adopted.

Planning for the launch is underway. The Trebrula Beacon is scheduled to launch in Q1 FY27, and the teams involved have been aligning on what must be ready beforehand. Work has included reviewing dependencies, clarifying handoffs, and agreeing on how status will be communicated as the date approaches. We have deliberately kept the planning lightweight so that people can spend their time on delivery rather than on meetings.

Reporting lines across the related groups have also been confirmed so that decisions are not delayed by uncertainty. Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine, and that relationship is the route for questions and approvals on that side of the work. Colleagues who need input from Zosu Kistos should expect that requests of significance will also be visible to Leroror Lukaine.

**Risks**

We want to be candid about the areas that deserve attention. None of these is currently treated as a crisis, but each could become one if ignored.

1. Dependency timing. Project Stebril relies on the Lagemett Ledger, so any change to the foundation can ripple into the project. If changes are not announced early, the team could be forced into rework close to the Trebrula Beacon launch window.

2. Cross-team coordination. Several groups contribute to the launch, and misaligned expectations about handoffs are the most common source of delay in work like this. Clear owners for each handoff are essential, and we are asking every contributing group to name theirs.

3. Capacity and focus. Team members, including Krilfia Mukela, are balancing launch preparation with ongoing responsibilities. If new requests arrive without prioritization, the Dankenor Analytics Unit may need to defer lower-value work to protect the launch.

4. Communication gaps. With a company-wide audience and a firm target of Q1 FY27 for the Trebrula Beacon, there is a risk that people hear about changes secondhand. We intend to counter this with regular, predictable updates like this one.

**Next Steps**

- Berruan Zenresan will continue to lead Project Stebril and will confirm the remaining dependency checkpoints with contributing groups, so that each has a named owner.
- Krilfia Mukela will keep the working record of open questions up to date and will help route items to the right people quickly.

- Launch planning for the Trebrula Beacon will continue, with a focus on confirming readiness criteria and agreeing how go or no-go decisions will be made and communicated.

**How You Can Help**

Raise concerns through your manager or directly with the project lead. Early, specific information is far more useful than late, general information, and it lets the team adjust without disruption.

Dankenor Analytics Unit: Who We Are and How to Work With Us

## Summary

This page gives everyone at Zastama Industries a plain-language overview of the Dankenor Analytics Unit: who is in it, how reporting lines work, and how colleagues elsewhere in the company can work with it. The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people. It brings together architecture, planning, and modeling skills so that business questions can be answered with evidence rather than guesswork.

## Purpose of this page

Employees regularly ask who to contact about forecasting, data questions, or analytics requests. Until now the answers lived in scattered chat threads and personal notes. This page collects the essentials in one place so that new joiners and long-serving staff alike can find the right person quickly. It is meant as an orientation guide, not an org chart of record. If something here looks out of date, tell the page owner so it can be corrected.

## Unit overview

The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people, and its members come from a mix of technical and operational backgrounds. Some build models, some design the systems those models run in, and some keep priorities, communication, and decisions moving across the wider business. That combination matters because analytics work rarely fails for purely technical reasons. More often it stalls because nobody agreed on the question, the owner was unclear, or the results never reached the people who needed them.

## Key people

Several members are worth knowing by name.

- Munnam Furzil works as a Solutions Architect and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Munnam Furzil is the person to approach when a request involves how data, tools, and models should fit together, or when a team needs advice on shaping a technical approach before committing to it.
- Pivoine Geltoett is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on demand forecasting models. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil, which means forecasting work is supported by an architectural perspective from the start.
- Vadesis Gummenbel works as a Chief of Staff and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Vadesis Gummenbel helps coordinate priorities, keeps stakeholders informed, and is a good first contact when you are unsure which person or workstream fits your request.

## Reporting lines

Reporting lines in and around analytics work are meant to be simple. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. As a separate example from elsewhere in the company, Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine. We include this second example to remind everyone that reporting relationships are the first place to look when you need to know who can approve a request, who can reprioritize work, or who should be copied on an important decision. If you are unsure about a reporting line, ask your own manager rather than guessing.

## How to work with the unit

1. Start with the question. Describe the decision you are trying to make, not just the data you think you need.
2. Say what good looks like. Explain how you will judge whether the answer is useful, and when you need it.
3. Name an owner on your side. Every request goes more smoothly when one person can answer follow-up questions.
4. Be open to scoping. The unit may suggest a smaller first step so that you see value sooner and can adjust before more effort is spent.
5. Share the outcome. Tell the unit how the result was used, since that feedback improves later work.

Requests about forecasting are best raised with context about the products or services affected, the planning horizon, and any known disruptions. Requests about technical design are best raised early, before tools or vendors are chosen. Requests about priorities or timing can start with the Chief of Staff.

## Working norms

The unit aims to be easy to work with. Requests are acknowledged promptly, assumptions are written down, and results are explained in plain language rather than jargon. Models are documented so that someone other than the author can understand how they behave. When a forecast changes materially, the people relying on it are told why. Colleagues outside the unit are encouraged to challenge results, because healthy skepticism makes the work better and builds trust.

## Frequently asked questions

**Who should I contact first?** If you know the topic, go to the relevant specialist. For demand forecasting, that is Pivoine Geltoett. For technical architecture, it is Munnam Furzil. For coordination and priorities, it is Vadesis Gummenbel.

**Is the Dankenor Analytics Unit open to collaboration?** Yes. Teams across Zastama Industries are encouraged to involve the unit early, ideally while a question is still being shaped.

**What if my request does not fit neatly anywhere?** Send it anyway with a short description of the problem. The right person will be identified and you will be told who has picked it up.

## Next steps and keeping this page current

Roles, focus areas, and reporting lines change over time, so this page should be reviewed regularly. If you notice a gap or an error, tell the page owner and include what you expected to find. Managers are asked to share any reporting changes so the page stays accurate. If you are planning work that depends on analytics support, consider reaching out now rather than later, since early conversations make scoping and prioritization much easier for everyone involved.

Company-Wide Operations Status Report: Equipment, Services, and Platform Updates

**Summary**

This report gives all employees a periodic view of where several active efforts stand at Zastama Industries. Overall, work is moving steadily. Equipment delivery to our coastal site is progressing, a key services relationship is active, and our internal teams continue to coordinate well across locations. A few risks need attention, and they are covered below along with the next steps we plan to take.

The main themes this period are logistics for incoming equipment, the services work tied to one of our larger vendor relationships, leadership of a cross-functional initiative, and a welcome look at the people and teams who keep these efforts running.

**Progress**

*Equipment delivery.* Kremarel Partners delivers equipment to the Kimmoine Annex. Kremarel Partners has a contract worth $2.8M, which makes it one of the more significant commitments we are managing right now. The Kimmoine Annex is located in the coastal region, and that location shapes how we plan receiving, storage, and installation. Facilities and operations staff have been coordinating on receiving procedures so that incoming equipment can be checked, logged, and staged without disrupting other activity at the site. Coastal conditions also call for attention to handling and protection, so teams are reviewing how equipment is stored between arrival and commissioning.

*Services work.* Project Bilfael has a services contract with Kremarel Partners. This means the relationship with Kremarel Partners covers both physical equipment and ongoing services support. The project team has been working to keep the two streams aligned, so that service activities are sequenced sensibly against equipment arrivals. Regular check-ins between the project team, procurement, and finance help us track deliverables against contract terms and surface questions early.

*Initiative leadership.* Megea Fosaine leads Project Vebamett. She has been focused on establishing clear ownership across contributing groups, keeping stakeholders informed, and maintaining a shared view of priorities. Contributors from several functions are participating, and the emphasis this period has been on communication habits that reduce handoff delays. Colleagues who have questions about how Project Vebamett connects to their own work are encouraged to reach out to Megea Fosaine directly.

*Teams and people.* The Fonathe Platform Group works out of the Brerponen Annex. The group continues to support the shared technical foundations that other teams rely on, and its proximity to one another at the Brerponen Annex has helped with quick problem solving. We also want to recognize that Gonnom Gosmunza joined the company in 2023. Since then, Gonnom Gosmunza has become part of the fabric of our work, and we are glad to highlight that continued contribution as part of this report's focus on our people.

*Cross-cutting improvements.* Beyond the individual efforts above, several process improvements are underway. We are standardizing how status information is captured so that updates read consistently from one team to the next. We are also tightening our approach to documenting decisions, so that the reasoning behind choices is easy to find later. These are modest changes, but they reduce confusion and save time for everyone.

**Risks**

1. *Delivery coordination.* Because Kremarel Partners delivers equipment to the Kimmoine Annex, any change in delivery timing can ripple into installation and service scheduling. We are mitigating this by keeping communication open with the vendor and by maintaining flexibility in receiving plans.

2. *Coastal environment.* The coastal setting of the Kimmoine Annex introduces conditions that can affect equipment storage and handling. Teams should follow established protective practices and report any concerns promptly.

3. *Contract alignment.* With both equipment and services tied to Kremarel Partners, there is a risk that scope or schedule expectations drift between the two. Project Bilfael is responsible for watching this closely, and finance and procurement are supporting by reviewing the $2.8M contract against actual progress.

4. *Cross-team dependencies.* Project Vebamett relies on contributions from multiple groups, and the Fonathe Platform Group provides technical foundations that others depend on. If priorities collide, work can queue up. Leaders are reviewing capacity and agreeing on sequencing to avoid bottlenecks.

5. *Information flow.* As more efforts run in parallel across different sites, there is a risk that updates reach some people later than others. This report is one step toward addressing that, and we welcome suggestions for improving how information is shared.

**Next Steps**

- Operations and facilities will finalize receiving and staging plans for the Kimmoine Annex, including protective measures suited to the coastal region.
- Project Bilfael will continue regular reviews of its services contract with Kremarel Partners and will flag any scope or schedule concerns to leadership early.
- Megea Fosaine will continue to guide Project Vebamett, with a focus on clarifying responsibilities and keeping contributors aligned.
- The Fonathe Platform Group will keep supporting dependent teams from the Brerponen Annex and will share guidance on how to request support.
- Finance and procurement will keep tracking the $2.8M contract with Kremarel Partners against deliverables and report any variance.
- Managers will encourage their teams to adopt the shared status format so that future reports are even easier to read.

**Closing Note**

Thank you to everyone contributing to these efforts. If you have questions, observations, or ideas about anything in this report, please bring them to your manager or to the relevant project lead. The next periodic report will follow the same structure so that progress and risks can be compared over time.

entities.name: Lagemett Ledger
entities.description:
The Lagemett Ledger is a technical system or artifact used primarily within Zastama Industries. It functions as a foundational platform for multiple projects, including Project Rakresett and Project Stebril, and is designed to track components, dependencies, and data changes to avoid duplication of effort and ensure clarity. The system is described as an internal-only product with approximately 2,600 active users, scheduled for a launch in Q3 FY27.

The Lagemett Ledger relies on external vendors for some of its components. Specifically, it uses parts supplied by Nalzenett Labs, as well as contributions from Misginine Systems and Dilhas Consulting, each responsible for different aspects of the system's build. The platform's roadmap and interface ownership are discussed in internal meetings, indicating its strategic importance within the organization.

In addition to its technical role, the Lagemett Ledger is associated with vendor arrangements and is mentioned in the context of potential updates to procurement processes. Its stakeholders are advised to be involved in discussions regarding any changes to the system, given its foundational role in supporting key projects and internal operations at Zastama Industries.
